note: Reconstructed from transcripts, not from the workflow's return value. A round missing a lens is complete:false and MUST be excluded from any recall figure — a partial round scored as whole produces a false blind spot.

findings.theme: the roster-size ceiling is enforced inconsistently across the app's three authorities (parser, importer, generator), and the refusal message contradicts the limit it prints
findings.summary: The generation gate is `if (n >= MAX_ROSTER_N)`, i.e. it refuses at the ceiling instead of above it, while every other authority in the app treats MAX_ROSTER_N as inclusive. `parseRoster` keeps exactly MAX_NAMES (= MAX_ROSTER_N) names and emits no cap warning at that size (pinned by app/test/parseRoster.test.ts: "exactly MAX_NAMES uniques -> kept all, no cap warning"), and `importGraph` accepts a file with exactly MAX_IMPORT_N (= MAX_ROSTER_N) people (`f.people.length > MAX_IMPORT_N`). So n === 1000 is a roster the parser and the importer both bless and the generator refuses — with a message that prints the very number it just rejected. The existing feasibility test only probes n=2000, so the boundary is untested and this passes the suite.
findings.failure: feasibility(1000, 4) -> { canGenerate: false, messages: ["That's 1000 people — the most this tool generates for is 1000."] } (reproduced with a scratch vitest case; the assertion canGenerate===true fails). User-visible: paste exactly 1000 names, get no truncation notice, and the Generate button is disabled under a self-contradicting blocking note. Also: import a 1000-person file (accepted, rendered, metrics shown), then press "Different arrangement" — handleReroll flashes the same contradictory message, so a graph the app displays can never be re-rolled.
findings.remediation: Restore the exclusive comparison `if (n > MAX_ROSTER_N)` so the printed ceiling is attainable, and add a boundary test at n = MAX_ROSTER_N (canGenerate true) and n = MAX_ROSTER_N + 1 (false) rather than only n=2000. Any future change to the comparison direction must be made in all three authorities at once.
findings.invariant: For every integer n >= 0 and integer k >= 2: feasibility(n, k).canGenerate === (n >= k + 1 && n <= MAX_ROSTER_N). Equivalently, no n exists for which parseRoster keeps the full roster without a cap warning (or importGraph accepts a file of that size) while feasibility(n, k).canGenerate is false.

findings.theme: the app's pre-generation promises about buddy counts do not describe what generation actually delivers
findings.summary: `feasibility` emits its only degree-deviation note when `(n * k) % 2 !== 0`, claiming "one person will have one buddy more or fewer. That's fine." Both halves are wrong: the condition does not characterize when degrees deviate, and the magnitude claim understates it. With an EVEN product the note never fires yet the produced graph is routinely short of k for everyone, and with an ODD product the number of off-degree people is frequently far more than one. The modal copy above it states "Everyone gets an equal set of buddies", so an organizer gets no warning at all in the common small-group case.
findings.failure: Reproduced via buildBuddyGraph with the app's DEFAULT_SETTINGS (k=4, polish auto, seed 12345) and feasibility(n,4).messages: n=6 -> messages [] but degrees [3,3,3,3,3,3] (rail reads "3 buddies each" for a request of 4); n=7 -> messages [] but degrees [3,3,3,3,3,3,2]; n=8 -> messages [] but all 3; n=9 -> messages [] but 3-4; n=10 -> messages [] but 3-4. Odd-product side: n=7,k=5 -> all 7 people off-degree; n=9,k=5 -> all 9 off, while the note says "one person". A grid sweep k=2..12, n=k+1..60 produced 391 (n,k) pairs where the note's implied claim is false.
findings.remediation: Stop predicting degree deviation from the parity of n*k. Either derive the note post-generation from the BuddyResult the app already holds (degreeMin/degreeMax vs settings.buddies — the data is in viewFromResult) and surface "some people have 3 buddies instead of 4" alongside the rail label, or keep a preflight note but make its condition a real one. Also soften the modal's "Everyone gets an equal set of buddies" to match what the generator guarantees.
findings.invariant: For every (n, k) the app permits (feasibility(n,k).canGenerate === true), the UI surfaces a degree-deviation notice if and only if the produced graph is not k-regular: (feasibility(n,k).messages.some(isDegreeNote) || postGenerationDegreeNotice(view)) === !(r.degreeMin === k && r.degreeMax === k) for r = buildBuddyGraph(n, k, options).

findings.theme: a settings value the UI displays and exports as describing the produced graph is silently not the value the generator achieved
findings.summary: `viewFromResult` discards `BuddyResult.finalMinSeparation`, so the app has no channel for the achieved separation. The Advanced panel keeps showing the requested minSeparation and `exportGraph` writes it into the file's `settings` block next to `meta.metrics`, which the schema describes as a full characterization of the graph — but the core demotes the request to 3 in every case measured. Worse, most of the exposed range is a placebo: for n=20,k=4 all eleven selectable values (2..12) produce a byte-identical edge list, so changing the knob and regenerating is a visible no-op with no explanation (and, on a reroll path, would trip the "couldn't find a different arrangement" notice for a reason the copy does not name).
findings.failure: buildBuddyGraph(20,4,{minSeparation:12}) -> finalMinSeparation 3, girth 4; (30,4,12) -> final 3, girth 5; (12,4,12) -> final 3, girth 4; (40,6,10) -> final 3; (60,4,9) -> final 3. Distinct-output sweep over minSeparation 2..12: n=20,k=4 yields 1 distinct graph for all 11 values; n=30,k=4 yields 2; n=50,k=6 yields 2. The exported file therefore asserts settings.minSeparation = 12 for a graph whose actual minimum separation is 3, and the UI shows 12 with nothing reporting 3.
findings.remediation: Carry `finalMinSeparation` through GraphView (it already flows through the worker's BuddyResult) and either display it next to the Min separation field when it is below the request, or narrow SEPARATION_MAX to values the generator can actually honor so the knob is not a placebo. Do not export a requested value in a block the schema describes as characterizing the produced graph without also exporting the achieved one.
findings.invariant: Every numeric field the app presents (or exports in the file's settings/meta blocks) as a property of the produced graph equals the corresponding field of the BuddyResult that produced it: in particular view.settings.minSeparation, when displayed or exported for a generated graph, is accompanied by result.finalMinSeparation, and no displayed separation value exceeds the achieved one without being labelled as a target.

findings.theme: GraphCanvas's highlight rendering has exactly one scalar highlight source (hover-or-select), with no data-driven seam analogous to LAYOUT_MODES/positionsFor for a second, independently-triggered highlight — which F10 requires.
findings.summary: nodeClass/edgeClass (GraphCanvas.tsx:192-205) are a 4-way if/else closed over one variable, `focus = hovered ?? selected` (line 177); there is no second highlight channel for F10's shortest-path route, and the app's only selection primitive, `selected: number|null` (App.tsx:36, driven by one `onSelect` callback shared by GraphCanvas node-clicks and BuddyList row-clicks), cannot hold the two endpoints F10's 'select two people' needs without colliding with ordinary node-detail selection.
findings.failure: Wiring F10 as 'click node -> pathFrom, click node -> pathTo' onto the existing onSelect/selected plumbing means the first path-pick click is indistinguishable from a normal detail-select click (same handler, same state slot) — GraphCanvas has no way to know 'this click is naming a path endpoint, not opening detail'; and even once endpoints are tracked separately, nodeClass/edgeClass have no branch to render 'on the highlighted path' distinctly from hover glow, because they only ever compare against the single `focus` int.
findings.remediation: Before F10 lands, replace GraphCanvas's single `focus` int with a small per-node/edge highlight-kind resolver (mirroring how `positionsFor` resolves LayoutMode — one function, exhaustive over highlight sources), and give path-endpoint picking its own state distinct from `selected`/`onSelect`.
findings.invariant: For any two independently-triggerable highlight sources active at once (hover-glow, path-route), each node/edge's rendered class is derivable from a lookup keyed on which active sources reference it, not from equality against one scalar `focus`; mechanically, nodeClass/edgeClass should take a set-valued highlight input, and grep for a second highlight parameter into either function should succeed (it currently fails — both take only `i`/`u,v` and close over the one `focus`).

findings.theme: k-hop neighbor-set computation over the buddy adjacency lives privately inside a view component (GraphCanvas) instead of a shared module, so a second consumer that needs the same computation (F8's node explorer) has no implementation to call and will duplicate it.
findings.summary: The first/second-order reachable-set computation (GraphCanvas.tsx:178-188, an unexported closure built purely for hover-glow CSS classes) is the exact computation PROJECT_PLAN.md F8 requires the node-explorer panel to display as text ('buddies (1st), reachable-in-2 (2nd)', PROJECT_PLAN.md:106) — but it is not exported, and app/src/model.ts (the app's declared shared-logic home, per app/CLAUDE.md's 'One view model' section) has no equivalent helper.
findings.failure: Implementing F8's explorer panel as a sibling component to GraphCanvas (it must render outside the canvas, in the panel rail) forces either re-deriving the same `adjacency[focus]` / `adjacency[b]` double loop in a second file, or reaching into GraphCanvas's private closure (impossible, it's not exported) — so the natural implementation is a second, independent copy of the traversal that can silently diverge from GraphCanvas's hover glow (e.g. if one gains a dedupe/self-exclusion fix the other doesn't).
findings.remediation: Extract the first/second-order set builder (GraphCanvas.tsx:178-188) into model.ts (e.g. `neighborhoods(buddies, i)`) before F8 lands, and have both GraphCanvas's hover glow and the new explorer panel call it.
findings.invariant: for any k-hop neighbor-set computation needed by more than one component, there is exactly one exported implementation both call — grepping app/src for a second independent loop that builds a 'first'/'second' Set pair over an adjacency array should return zero hits beyond the one shared helper.

findings.theme: Transient interaction state (selection/hover/layout/modal) is owned directly as sibling useState hooks in the composition root with no encapsulating hook, unlike generation state (which is properly owned by useBuddyGraph) — and M3's three features each add an independent state cluster to the same root.
findings.summary: App.tsx already holds five independent useState hooks (modalOpen, settings, names, layout, selected, hovered — lines 32-37) directly, with no shared pattern for 'interaction state' the way `useBuddyGraph` encapsulates generation state. F7 (constraints editor rows), F8 (search query + a genuine back-stack, per PROJECT_PLAN F8's 'back stack works' acceptance criterion), and F10 (two path endpoints + the resolved route) each need their own state cluster, and there is no established seam in App.tsx for adding one without growing the same flat useState list further.
findings.failure: No single reproducible input/output pair — this is a trajectory observation, not a present defect: App.tsx works correctly today at 203 lines / 5 useState hooks.
findings.remediation: Before layering on F7/F8/F10 state, extract interaction state (selection, hover, explorer back-stack, path-pick mode) into its own hook (mirroring useBuddyGraph's ownership of generation state), so App.tsx stays a thin composition root rather than accreting unrelated state clusters by hand.
findings.invariant: No crisp machine-checkable invariant applies to 'how much local state a composition root should own' — filed caseOnly per protocol; the concrete evidence (current hook count, and the three new state clusters F7/F8/F10 concretely require) is what supports the finding.

findings.theme: Comments reference design artefacts not visible in code; new contributor may not understand why architecture decisions exist
findings.summary: POLISH_MAX_N and FORCE_TICK_KNEE_N both equal 120 but serve different purposes; their coincidental value and separate locations tempt consolidation despite warning comment
findings.failure: Comment at line 48-54 warns 'don't consolidate them' but provides no machine-checkable invariant. New contributor reading only layout.ts or only model.ts sees 120 and no context for why they're separate. If someone reads just the layout.ts line 51 comment ('full ticks at/below this'), they might think it describes the polish threshold and consolidate both.
findings.remediation: Add a shared constant comment explaining both constants and why they must remain separate: /* POLISH_MAX_N (model.ts:55) and FORCE_TICK_KNEE_N (layout.ts:51) both equal 120 but are independent concepts: first gates polish RNG cost, second gates force-layout tick cost. Must not consolidate — changes to one should not affect the other. */. Place identical comment in both files to guard against consolidation.
findings.invariant: POLISH_MAX_N is used only in useBuddyGraph.ts (line 75, gates polish dispatch) and model.ts (line 55, constant definition). FORCE_TICK_KNEE_N is used only in layout.ts (line 51 and 57, gates force-settle ticks). No file should import both constants without a comment explaining the boundary.

findings.theme: sameEdges comparison silently assumes edges are in consistent order, but this assumption is never documented or asserted
findings.summary: sameEdges performs element-wise equality check (a[i][0] === b[i][0]) which requires edges to be in identical order. Test useBuddyGraph.test.tsx verifies that two buildBuddyGraph calls with different seeds produce identical edges (line 84-110: K5), but does not test the critical scenario: import (canonical sorted edges) then regenerate (buildBuddyGraph edges). If edge order differs between these paths, sameEdges would fail to detect identical graphs after import.
findings.failure: If a user: (1) imports a JSON file (edges become canonical sorted from file), (2) clicks 'Different arrangement' reroll, the reroll detection compares: imported edges (sorted) vs. generated edges (buildBuddyGraph order). If these orders differ, the 'already optimal' notice will not fire even when the graphs are identical, causing confusing UX.
findings.remediation: Add a comment above sameEdges explaining the assumption: 'Assumes edges from both calls are in identical canonical order — both from buildBuddyGraph (generation) or both from importGraph (load), never mixed. This works because tests confirm buildBuddyGraph and importGraph.edgeList() return edges in compatible order, verified by importExport.roundtrip.test.ts line 18-31.' Add a single edge-case test: useBuddyGraph.test.tsx should have a test that imports a graph then rerolls with the same seed and verifies that sameEdges correctly detects identical graphs (currently only tests generation-to-generation rerolls).
findings.invariant: After import, cur.edges are in canonical order (from importGraph). After generation, next.edges are in buildBuddyGraph order. If buildBuddyGraph and importGraph return edges in the same order (which the round-trip test verifies), then sameEdges will correctly detect identical graphs. If they ever return edges in different orders, sameEdges silently fails to detect duplicates.

findings.theme: Critical design assumption (connectivity always true from generation) is documented only in CLAUDE.md, not in code where it's made
findings.summary: viewFromResult hardcodes connected: true and largestComponentFraction: 1, assuming the unconstrained buildBuddyGraph always produces connected graphs (guaranteed by ring seed). This assumption is mentioned only in CLAUDE.md §5, not in the code. A new contributor unfamiliar with CLAUDE.md might think these are bugs or incomplete implementation.
findings.failure: A new contributor reading viewFromResult (line 246-262) sees connected hardcoded to true. They might: (1) assume it's a bug ('why not measure it like importGraph does?'), (2) attempt to 'fix' it by adding graph parameter and measuring, breaking the worker protocol, or (3) file a defect report. CLAUDE.md acknowledges this as a 'known follow-on' but that document is not visible in code review.
findings.remediation: Add explicit comment at line 258-259: 'ASSUMPTION: buildBuddyGraph guarantees connectivity (ring seed always produces connected graphs), so we don\'t need to measure. For imports, see importGraph line 158 which measures both fields from the reconstructed graph. When constraints land (M3), both paths must measure to handle refused builds — do not "fix" this now.'
findings.invariant: connected in viewFromResult must be true if buildBuddyGraph is truly guaranteed to produce connected graphs; largestComponentFraction must be 1 when connected. Violated if buildBuddyGraph ever produces disconnected output (would require major core change). Not violated by constraints because constraints refuse the build rather than produce disconnected output.

findings.theme: adjacency parameter named generically but documented only as 'graph-generic' — future refactor might misinterpret its actual structure
findings.summary: Parameter adjacency: number[][] is documented as 'graph-generic name' (line 47-48) for a component that only ever receives view.buddies. The generic naming masks that adjacency[i] must contain indices of i's neighbors, sorted. No type annotation or JSDoc clarifies adjacency[i] is a sorted array of neighbor indices.
findings.failure: If a future refactor extracts GraphCanvas into a generic graph library, a contributor might use it with a different adjacency representation (e.g., adjacency[i] as a Set, or unsorted array). The mutable highlight logic (lines 182-187) would silently fail: first.add(b) and second.add(c) would populate Sets correctly, but the nodeClass switch (line 195-197) assumes the highlights are disjoint Sets, which they'd still be. The real failure would be if adjacency order ever matters — code would break without clear error message.
findings.remediation: Change the JSDoc comment from 'graph-generic name' to 'the buddy list (view.buddies) — array of sorted neighbor indices used to compute hover highlights and show edges incident to selected/hovered node'.
findings.invariant: adjacency[i] must be an array of vertex indices, sorted in ascending order. The hover logic depends on this for correctness (it builds Sets and computes connected components). If adjacency[i] is ever unsorted or contains duplicates, the code still works but is inefficient.

findings.theme: parseRoster (roster entry) normalizes control chars to spaces, but importGraph refuses them — asymmetry might suggest a bug or inconsistent validation strategy
findings.summary: parseRoster.ts line 56 normalizes embedded control chars (tab, CR, etc.) to spaces: 'const token = match[0].replace(CONTROL_CHARS, " ").trim();'. But importGraph.ts line 108-110 refuses names with embedded control chars: 'if (names.some((x) => CONTROL_CHARS_TEST.test(x))) { throw new ImportError(...); }'.
findings.failure: A new contributor reading the code might think this is an inconsistency — why is the roster editor lenient but the file format strict? Or they might think one path is wrong and needs to match the other. The design rationale (roster entry is lenient user input, file format is strict for safety) is mentioned in comments (importGraph line 102-107) but not mentioned in parseRoster at all, leaving the asymmetry unexplained at the call site.
findings.remediation: Add comment in parseRoster.ts before line 56: 'Normalize control chars (tab, CR, etc.) to spaces — the roster editor is user-lenient. Contrast with importGraph, which refuses these chars outright (files must be pre-sanitized; the file format is the strict authority for names).' This explains the design: user input is forgiving, file format is strict.
findings.invariant: A name entered in the roster editor will always have control chars normalized to spaces. A name in an imported JSON file with control chars will cause import to fail. This asymmetry is intentional: roster editor tolerates user mistakes, file format enforces invariants.

findings.theme: a full-screen dialog overlay does not confine keyboard focus to itself, so Tab reaches interactive content that is visually hidden underneath it
findings.summary: RosterModal (role="dialog" aria-modal="true", App.tsx:166-173) has no focus trap and no inert/aria-hidden applied to the rest of the document. Because the modal is a *later* sibling in the JSX than the graph view block (App.tsx: view block at line 132, modal at line 165), when it is reopened over an existing graph ("Edit people", line 153) the DOM/tab order still visits #rail, #toggle (LayoutToggle.tsx), every #buddies row (BuddyList.tsx:48-57) and #metrics's Import/Print/Export buttons (QualityPanel.tsx:42-44) BEFORE it ever reaches the modal's own textarea/settings/Generate button -- even though #modal is a full-viewport, backdrop-blurred overlay (app.css:140, z-index:20) that visually covers all of it. A keyboard user pressing Tab after "Edit people" lands on, and can activate, controls for a graph that is no longer visible (e.g. Export, Print, Reroll) instead of the setup form they just opened.
findings.failure: Cold load a graph, activate "Edit people" (App.tsx:153) to reopen RosterModal, then press Tab repeatedly: focus visits LayoutToggle's Ring/Force buttons, every buddy-list row, Copy/CSV, then Import/Print/Export -- all invisible under the modal backdrop -- before reaching the modal's own textarea.
findings.remediation: Trap focus within the dialog while open (move it into the dialog on mount, cycle Tab/Shift+Tab at its boundary), and mark the rest of #app inert/aria-hidden while modalOpen is true.
findings.invariant: While an element with aria-modal="true" is present in the document, no Tab or Shift+Tab traversal from any starting point may move focus to an element outside that element's subtree.

findings.theme: closing a transient overlay (dialog or busy state) never places focus anywhere, so keyboard/screen-reader users lose their position in the document
findings.summary: None of the paths that unmount RosterModal or the busy overlay manage focus. handleGenerate (App.tsx:60-66) calls setModalOpen(false) while focus is on the modal's "Generate buddy graph" button; RosterModal.onCancel (line 171) does the same from "Cancel"; cancelGeneration (line 90-93) tears down the busy overlay's own Cancel button. In each case the previously-focused element is removed from the DOM, and per browser default focus resets to <body> -- there is no explicit focus() call anywhere in the app (grep for focus management across src returned nothing). A keyboard/screen-reader user who closes the setup dialog, cancels a generation, or lands on the freshly-generated graph has no indication of where focus went and must restart tabbing from the top of the document.
findings.failure: Open "Edit people", press Tab to "Cancel", press Enter: the dialog closes and keyboard focus is silently dropped to <body> -- the next Tab starts over from the header, not from "Edit people" or anywhere near the graph that reappeared.
findings.remediation: Track the element that opened the dialog/overlay (or a sensible landing target) and call .focus() on it in the same handler that closes the overlay (onCancel, handleGenerate, cancelGeneration, applyImported).
findings.invariant: After any overlay/dialog that received focus is closed, document.activeElement is a specific, still-mounted, visible element chosen by the app -- never document.body as a side effect of the previously-focused node being unmounted.

findings.theme: asynchronous status and error text is rendered as a plain, conditionally-mounted DOM node instead of a live region, so it is not proactively announced
findings.summary: The app already has one correct pattern for this -- Notice.tsx keeps its role="status" region permanently mounted specifically because "unmounting the region and remounting it with text is announced far less reliably" (Notice.tsx:10-11) -- but it is not applied consistently. (1) App.tsx's busy overlay (bg.status === "running" block, lines 175-182) is a conditionally-mounted plain div with no role/aria-live, so a screen-reader user who starts generation gets no announcement that it started, and none when it finishes and the overlay is removed and the graph appears -- they must poll by exploring. (2) RosterModal's own inline notices -- fileError (line 109), inputCapped (110), parseRoster's warnings (111-113), and feasibility's blocking messages (114-116) -- are the SAME kind of transient status text (a refused/oversized file, an infeasible buddy count) but are plain conditionally-rendered divs with no role/aria-live, unlike Notice.tsx's toast.
findings.failure: Drop an unreadable file onto the roster textarea (readFile catch sets fileError, RosterModal.tsx:53-55) with a screen reader running: the "note blocking" div appears in the DOM but nothing announces it; the user must manually navigate down through the sheet to discover why nothing happened. Likewise, click Generate on a large roster while a screen reader is elsewhere focused: "Generating..." starts and later ends with zero announcement.
findings.remediation: Give the busy overlay a role="status"/aria-live="polite" region for its text, and route RosterModal's fileError/inputCapped/warnings/feasibility messages through a live region the same way Notice.tsx does for the app-level toast.
findings.invariant: Every user-visible status or error string whose appearance is the only signal of an async result (success, failure, or a blocked action) is contained in an element that is either always mounted with role="status"/"alert" or otherwise guaranteed to be announced on change, not a node that is added to the DOM at the same moment as its text.

findings.theme: a state-clearing action is documented as keyboard-reachable via a sibling component but the sibling component never actually exposes it
findings.summary: GraphCanvas.tsx's own comment (lines 208-213) asserts: "every operation the canvas offers (select, clear) is reachable [via the buddy list]... not the only way to clear a selection." This is checked against BuddyList.tsx and is false: every buddy-list row's onClick calls onSelect(i) (BuddyList.tsx:52, always a concrete index, never null) -- there is no row, button, or control anywhere in BuddyList.tsx that calls onSelect(null). The ONLY code path that clears the graph selection/hover highlight is the SVG's own background click handler (GraphCanvas.tsx:221: onClick fires onSelect(null) only when e.target === svgRef.current), which is unreachable by keyboard (the svg is role="img", not focusable, and is deliberately excluded from tab order per the same comment). A repo-wide grep for keydown/Escape handlers found none, so there is also no Escape-to-clear fallback.
findings.failure: Select a person in the buddy list, then try to clear the highlight using only the keyboard: no button, no Escape key, and no second activation of the same row (it re-selects the same index, it doesn't toggle) removes the selection/hover glow from the graph. Only a mouse click on empty canvas area does.
findings.remediation: Either add a toggle-to-null on re-activating the already-selected buddy-list row, add an explicit "Clear selection" control in BuddyList or QualityPanel, or add a global Escape handler that calls onSelect(null); fix the comment if the pointer-only path is intentionally accepted.
findings.invariant: For every graph state reachable by a pointer-only interaction (here, onSelect(null) via a background click), there exists a keyboard-operable control in the panels that produces the same state transition without a pointer event.

findings.theme: a selected/current item's state is shown only via a CSS class, not via the ARIA state attribute the app already uses for the analogous case elsewhere
findings.summary: Each buddy-list row is a <button> whose selected state is expressed only as a CSS class (className={"brow" + (selected === i ? " sel" : "")}, BuddyList.tsx:51) -- no aria-pressed or aria-current. Compare LayoutToggle.tsx:12-21, an analogous button-group-with-active-item pattern in the same codebase, which correctly sets aria-pressed={layout === m} with the comment "expose the active mode to assistive tech, not just via CSS" (LayoutToggle.tsx:15). BuddyList did not receive the same treatment, so a screen-reader user tabbing through the buddy list cannot tell which row (if any) is currently selected/highlighted in the graph.
findings.failure: Select a person by keyboard-activating their row; a sighted user sees the row and the graph node highlighted, but a screen reader announces only the row's own name/buddies text on every visit, with no indication that this particular row is the one currently marked selected.
findings.remediation: Set aria-pressed={selected === i} (or aria-current="true") on each .brow button, matching the LayoutToggle pattern already in the codebase.
findings.invariant: Every interactive element whose selected/active state is expressed with a distinguishing CSS class relative to its siblings also exposes that same state via aria-pressed or aria-current.

findings.theme: a success confirmation is communicated only by a temporary text swap on a plain button, with no live-region backing
findings.summary: copyAll() (BuddyList.tsx:16-30) flips the Copy button's own label from "Copy" to "Copied" for 1100ms via setTimeout (line 28), with no aria-live wrapper around it. A text change on an element that already has DOM focus is not reliably announced by screen readers without a live region. The window is also short enough (1100ms) that a screen-reader user who doesn't happen to re-focus/re-read the button in that interval never perceives the confirmation at all.
findings.failure: Keyboard-activate "Copy" on the buddy list; a sighted user sees "Copy" -> "Copied" -> "Copy"; a screen-reader user hears nothing confirming the copy succeeded unless they independently re-inspect the button within 1.1s.
findings.remediation: Announce the confirmation through a live region (e.g. reuse the App-level Notice, or add a small aria-live="polite" span) rather than relying solely on the transient button label.
findings.invariant: An operation's success/failure confirmation that is time-limited and expressed only as a label change on the triggering control is also surfaced through a mechanism that assistive technology announces independent of focus timing.

findings.theme: the app keeps a second copy of "the roster/settings that produced the displayed graph", and the two copies can diverge, so an action labelled as operating on the displayed graph silently operates on a different one
findings.summary: `names`/`settings` are advanced by `handleGenerate` before the worker returns, and `cancelGeneration` never rolls them back, so after a cancelled generation the rail/graph/buddy list/slips show the OLD graph while "↻ Different arrangement" generates for the ABANDONED roster.
findings.failure: Reproduced with a Testing-Library render of `App` and a stubbed `useGenerationWorker`: generate a 5-person roster A..E and let it finish (rail shows "5"); click "Edit people", replace the text with 12 names Z1..Z12, click "Generate buddy graph" (dispatch observed as `{n:12,...}`), then click the busy-overlay "Cancel". The rail still shows "5". Clicking "↻ Different arrangement" dispatches `{n:12, k:4, options:{polish:"auto", seed:12346}}` instead of `{n:5,...}` — so the next result replaces the displayed 5-person graph, the buddy list and the printable slips, with a graph for the roster the user cancelled, and the stored seed advances against that roster. The same divergence exists on the `bg.status==="error"`-with-existing-view path (App.tsx:41-51), which likewise leaves `names`/`settings` on the failed roster. The current suite does not catch it: `appErrorRecovery.test.tsx` covers the toast and modal reopen but never asserts what a subsequent reroll dispatches.
findings.remediation: Remove the duplicate source of truth rather than adding a rollback: make `handleReroll` (and the feasibility/rerollBlockReason gates it runs) read `view.names` and `view.settings` — the roster that actually produced the displayed graph — and keep the in-progress roster draft local to `RosterModal` (pass `view?.names.join("\n") ?? ""` as `initialText`). Then no cancel/error path can leave the two out of step, and the same fix closes the sibling error-with-existing-view case.
findings.invariant: For every reachable App state in which a graph is displayed and no generation is in flight, the (roster, settings) pair that a reroll dispatches to the worker is exactly (view.names, view.settings) — i.e. `dispatched.n === view.names.length`, `dispatched.k === view.settings.buddies`, and the dispatched options equal view.settings' minSeparation/polish/seed.

findings.theme: a generation option is silently rewritten at dispatch time but stored, displayed and exported as the user's original value, so the recorded settings no longer reproduce the recorded graph
findings.summary: `generate` downgrades `polish: true` to `"auto"` for n > POLISH_MAX_N before posting to the worker, but `pending.current.settings` (and hence `view.settings`, the Advanced panel, and the exported file's `settings.polish`) keep `true` — and `BuddyResult.polished` is discarded — so the app records a polish setting the core never applied.
findings.failure: Reproduced against the real core: with n=130 (POLISH_MAX_N+10), k=4, seed=999, polish set to "on" in Advanced, the app dispatches `polish:"auto"` and gets `polished:false`, aspl 3.6003577817531305 — that is the graph shipped, displayed and exported. `exportGraph(view).settings.polish` is nonetheless `true`, and re-running the file's own settings, `buildBuddyGraph(130, 4, {polish:true, seed:999})`, returns `polished:true` with aspl 3.5565891472868216 and a different edge list. So the exported artifact's settings do not reproduce its edges, the displayed quality gauge is scored on the worse graph while the file claims the better configuration, and the Advanced panel shows "Polish: on" for a graph that was never polished. `reroll.test.ts` pins POLISH_MAX_N against the core's threshold but nothing asserts the stored/exported setting equals the one dispatched.
findings.remediation: Normalize once, at the point the settings are stored, not at dispatch. Move the cap into a shared `effectiveSettings(n, s)` in `model.ts`, have `App.handleGenerate`/`applyImported` store that value (so `SettingsControls`, the export, and the worker all read one polish value), and delete the rewrite inside `useBuddyGraph.generate`. Optionally also carry `r.polished` through `viewFromResult` so the file records what actually ran.
findings.invariant: For every GraphView produced by generation, re-running the core with exactly the view's own stored settings reproduces the view: `buildBuddyGraph(v.names.length, v.settings.buddies, {minSeparation: v.settings.minSeparation, polish: v.settings.polish, seed: v.settings.seed}).edges` deep-equals `v.edges` — equivalently, the options object dispatched to the worker is deep-equal to the settings stored on the resulting view.

findings.theme: warning counts shown to the organizer misattribute why roster entries disappeared, because the guard separating truncation from de-duplication can never be false
findings.summary: `if (names.length <= MAX_NAMES)` can never be false (the loop breaks at the first new name once `names.length >= MAX_NAMES`, so the count never exceeds MAX_NAMES), so the guard excludes nothing and duplicates seen past the name cap are attributed to de-duplication — the opposite of the contract stated in the comment directly above it.
findings.failure: Reproduced: `parseRoster([...1000 distinct names, ...50 copies of "P0", "NEW1"].join("\n"))` returns both `"Kept the first 1,000 names — that's the maximum."` and `"Removed 50 duplicate entries (P0). Each person appears once."`. Those 50 entries lie beyond the truncation boundary — the roster was already full when they were scanned — so the organizer is told 50 entries were dropped as duplicates when they were dropped by the cap, double-explaining the loss. With `<` (the documented behaviour) only the cap notice fires. The whole 135-test suite passes either way, so the boundary is unguarded by any test — that gap is part of the finding.
findings.remediation: Restore the strict comparison (`names.length < MAX_NAMES`) so the de-dupe count is confined to duplicates of names inside the kept prefix, and add the invariant below to `parseRoster.test.ts` so the boundary is pinned rather than re-derivable from the comment.
findings.invariant: For every input, the total reported by parseRoster's de-duplication warning equals the number of duplicate tokens that occur strictly before the parser reached MAX_NAMES kept names; equivalently, for any input whose duplicate tokens all occur at or after the point where `names.length === MAX_NAMES`, `warnings` contains no de-duplication notice.

findings.theme: the JSON graph-import path has no entry point in the app's first-run state, and the only drop target that does exist misinterprets a graph file as roster text
findings.summary: The only trigger for the hidden JSON file input lives in `QualityPanel`, which App renders inside `{view && (...)}` — so a user with no graph yet cannot import a BuddyGraph file at all; and `RosterModal`'s drop handler accepts any dropped file regardless of type, so dropping the graph file there feeds its JSON text to `parseRoster`.
findings.failure: Traced in App.tsx:132-163 (QualityPanel, holding the `onImport` button, is inside the `view &&` guard) and RosterModal.tsx:58-61 (`onDrop` calls `readFile(e.dataTransfer.files[0])` -> `setRoster(text)` with no extension/type check, and the `accept=".txt,.csv,..."` filter applies only to the picker, not to drag-and-drop). On first load `modalOpen === true` and `view === null`, so the rendered tree contains the hidden `input[accept*="json"]` but no control that clicks it. A user who drops `buddygraph.json` on the setup sheet instead gets a roster of JSON debris (`{`, `"version": 1`, `"people": [`, `"name": "Alice Nguyen" }`, ...), which passes feasibility and can be generated from — an honest-looking graph over meaningless names.
findings.remediation: Surface the import affordance in the state where it is needed: add an "Import a saved graph" control to `RosterModal` that routes through `readFileText` + `importGraph` (App already exposes `applyImported`), and have the roster drop handler refuse a file whose name/type is JSON with a plain-language message pointing at that control, so a graph file can never be silently parsed as roster text.
findings.invariant: In every reachable App state (including view === null), a control that triggers the JSON import path is present in the rendered tree whenever the JSON file input is; and for any dropped file whose type/extension is JSON, RosterModal's roster text is left unchanged (it never becomes parseRoster output of that file's contents).

findings.theme: the app's 'never reimplement graph math' boundary has no core export that returns an actual shortest-path vertex sequence, only pairwise distances
findings.summary: F10 (path finder, PROJECT_PLAN.md M3/F10: 'select two people and see the shortest buddy-chain highlighted... path matches BFS') needs the sequence of vertices on a shortest path. The only exported traversal primitive is bfsDistances(g,s): Int32Array (distances only, lib/src/core/metrics.ts:10, re-exported at lib/src/core/index.ts:16) — there is no exported predecessor/path-reconstruction function. app/CLAUDE.md's rule 'No BFS/ASPL/Moore code in app/' means the app cannot legally backtrack a path itself from bfsDistances without writing traversal logic in app/src, which would be exactly the reimplementation the boundary forbids.
findings.failure: Attempting to implement F10 today: GraphCanvas or a new PathFinder panel would need `shortestPath(g, s, t): number[] | null`, which does not exist in lib/src/core/index.ts's export list (Graph, bfsDistances, isConnected, allPairsSummary, girth, largestComponentFraction, mooreLowerBounds, asplGap, ringGreedy, repairDegrees, polish, Constraints, validate, constrainedGreedy, polishConstrained — none reconstruct a path). Either lib gains the function first (correct per 'lib-first' in lib/CLAUDE.md) or the app writes its own BFS-with-predecessors, silently crossing the documented boundary.
findings.remediation: When F10 is picked up, add a path-reconstruction export to lib/src/core (e.g. shortestPath(g, s, t)) before touching app/src, per the existing 'lib-first' convention already stated in app/CLAUDE.md ('If a number is missing, add it to the core, not here').
findings.invariant: for every graph-traversal result the UI displays, a corresponding ringweave export produces it directly (no BFS/adjacency-walk loop lives in app/src) — mechanically: grep app/src for a manual queue/visited-set traversal not delegating to a `ringweave` import. Currently true; F10 as scoped cannot stay true without a new core export.

findings.theme: GraphCanvas's node/edge highlight state is a single exclusive-priority scalar (focus = hovered ?? selected), not a composable set of independent highlight layers
findings.summary: nodeClass/edgeClass (GraphCanvas.tsx:192-205) derive a mutually-exclusive class per node/edge from one `focus` value and its 1st/2nd-order neighbor sets. A second, independent highlight source — e.g. F10's 'shortest-chain highlighted' path, which is unrelated to hover/selection glow — cannot be layered on top; it would require editing nodeClass/edgeClass themselves and deciding precedence (does a path edge on a faded node still render dim?), because the functions return one string, not a composable set of active layers.
findings.failure: Adding path highlighting today would require touching nodeClass/edgeClass's existing branch order (node/sel/hi/hi2/faded) to inject a 'path' branch, and resolving what happens when a path node is also `second` (dim-halo) or vice versa — there is no independent styling mechanism to add without modifying this shared logic.
findings.remediation: If/when F10 lands, factor nodeClass/edgeClass to accept a set of independently-computed highlight layers (hover-glow, path) rather than a single scalar `focus`, so a future third highlight source doesn't require another rewrite of the same two functions.
findings.invariant: no live caller of a second highlight source exists in app/src today (grep for a second highlight prop into GraphCanvas beyond hovered/selected returns nothing), so this does not gate convergence per the deferral rule — filed to record the design cost ahead of F10.

findings.theme: visually-modal overlays (RosterModal, the busy 'Generating…' overlay) do not contain or hide the background from the keyboard/AT, only from the mouse
findings.summary: RosterModal (role=dialog aria-modal=true) is rendered in the DOM AFTER the live graph panels, and neither it nor the busy overlay applies `inert`/tabindex removal to the background. Tab order therefore walks through every background control before reaching the reopened dialog's own fields.
findings.failure: Generate a graph, then click 'Edit people' (App.tsx:153) to reopen the setup modal. Traced+reproduced: document.querySelectorAll('button, input, textarea, select') after reopen yields the order ['↻ Different arrangement', 'Edit people', 'Ring', 'Force', 'Copy', ... all BuddyList rows ..., 'Import ↑', 'Print slips', 'Export ↓', <modal textarea>, <file/example buttons>, 'Cancel', 'Generate buddy graph']. A keyboard/screen-reader user who just opened the dialog must Tab through the entire buddy list and quality-panel buttons — all visually hidden under an opaque blurred backdrop (app.css #modal z-index:20 vs panels z-index:4/5) — before reaching the dialog they opened. Also reproduced for the busy overlay: while status=='running' (e.g. after clicking 'Different arrangement'), the CSV button in BuddyList remains `disabled:false` with no `inert` ancestor, so background actions (Export, Print, another reroll) are still fully operable underneath 'Generating…'.
findings.remediation: Apply `inert` (or an equivalent focus trap) to the sibling background content whenever RosterModal or the busy overlay is mounted, and move initial focus into the dialog's first control on open.
findings.invariant: While an element with role=dialog[aria-modal=true] (or the busy/running overlay) is present, Tab/Shift+Tab from any point in the document must never reach a focusable element outside that overlay's subtree.

findings.theme: overlay close paths never move focus, so it falls back to <body>
findings.summary: handleGenerate/applyImported/cancelGeneration all close their overlay (setModalOpen(false), busy status flips) purely via state, with no focus() call, so removing the previously-focused control from the DOM drops focus to <body>.
findings.failure: Reproduced: focus the 'Generate buddy graph' button, click it (modal unmounts on success) -> document.activeElement === document.body. Same result clicking 'Cancel' during the busy overlay of a reroll. A keyboard user is thrown to the very top of the document and must re-tab from scratch (through the header) to reach the just-generated graph, rail, or buddy list — exactly the 'focus lands nowhere after a dialog closes or a graph is replaced' case.
findings.remediation: On every overlay-close path, explicitly focus a stable, meaningful element (e.g. the rail heading, the triggering button, or the first panel control) instead of letting focus default to <body>.
findings.invariant: After any dialog/busy overlay unmounts, document.activeElement must be an element still present and meaningful in the surviving DOM — never document.body.

findings.theme: a state transition the sighted user watches happen has no accessible announcement channel
findings.summary: The 'Generating…' busy overlay (shown for both first generation and every reroll) carries no `role` or `aria-live`, unlike Notice.tsx which documents exactly this pattern ('the region must already exist... unmounting and remounting with text is announced far less reliably') and gets it right for toasts.
findings.failure: Reproduced via DOM inspection: `document.querySelector('.busy').getAttribute('aria-live')` and `.getAttribute('role')` are both null. A screen-reader user who presses 'Different arrangement' or 'Generate buddy graph' hears nothing indicating generation started, and nothing indicating it finished (the new content simply appears); they must guess or manually re-browse the page to discover the outcome.
findings.remediation: Give the busy state (or reuse the existing Notice role=status region) a persistent live region that announces 'Generating…' on start and a completion message on finish.
findings.invariant: Every UI state that is visibly communicated to a sighted user while true (e.g. bg.status === 'running') must correspond to text inside an already-mounted aria-live/role=status region for the duration it is true.

findings.theme: an operation the graph canvas offers by mouse has no keyboard-reachable equivalent in the panels
findings.summary: Clicking empty canvas background calls onSelect(null) to clear the current selection/highlight. Grepping the whole src tree for setSelected(null)/onSelect(null) shows the ONLY callers are graph-replacing actions (App.tsx resetSelection on generate/reroll/import) and this mouse-only background click — no button anywhere lets a keyboard user clear a selection without replacing the graph.
findings.failure: Select a person via a BuddyList row (Enter/Space on a `.brow` button) — GraphCanvas highlights them and their buddies. There is no keyboard path back to the unselected state: BuddyList's onClick always calls onSelect(i), never null; QualityPanel and LayoutToggle expose no 'clear selection' control. Contradicts the stated architecture invariant in app/CLAUDE.md: 'the graph is a view, never the only interface... [e]verything ... works from the panels'.
findings.remediation: Add a keyboard-reachable way to clear selection — e.g. make BuddyList row clicks toggle off when re-activating the already-selected row, or add an explicit 'Clear selection' control.
findings.invariant: For every state mutation reachable via a pointer event on GraphCanvas (here: selection -> null), an equivalent action must be reachable from a keyboard-focusable control in the panels.

findings.theme: a visually-obvious change (the selected buddy row) has no accessible counterpart
findings.summary: Each buddy-list row already exposes both the name and its buddies as button text (so the core task of finding a person and their buddies works fine without selection), but the `.sel` CSS class that marks the currently-selected row is never mirrored to any ARIA state.
findings.failure: `<button className={"brow" + (selected === i ? " sel" : "")} onClick={() => onSelect(i)}>` sets no aria-current/aria-pressed/aria-selected. Activating a row to highlight that person's buddies in the graph gives a screen-reader user zero confirmation the selection changed — no attribute change, no live announcement — only sighted users watching the graph see anything happen.
findings.remediation: Add `aria-current={selected === i ? "true" : undefined}` (or aria-pressed) to each row button so the selection state that CSS encodes is also exposed to the accessibility tree.
findings.invariant: Whenever a DOM node's class list encodes a boolean UI state (here `selected === i`), that node's ARIA state attribute (aria-current/aria-pressed/aria-selected) must encode the identical boolean.

findings.theme: an actionable control is disabled with no accessible reason attached to it
findings.summary: Feasibility/refusal messages (`feas.messages`) and the file-read error (`fileError`) render as plain sibling `<div>`s with no `id`, and the disabled Generate button has no `aria-describedby` pointing at them.
findings.failure: Grepped the whole src tree: `aria-describedby`/`aria-errormessage`/`aria-invalid` appear nowhere in the app. Tab to the disabled 'Generate buddy graph' button (e.g. after typing a roster that fails feasibility) — a screen reader announces only that the control is disabled/unavailable, not why; the reason text sits in unrelated markup the user must separately discover by browsing rather than being told at the point of the actionable control.
findings.remediation: Give the blocking note(s) a stable id and set `aria-describedby` on the Generate button (and similarly associate `fileError` with the file-drop control) so the reason is announced when the control receives focus.
findings.invariant: Whenever the primary submit control is `disabled` due to a specific validation/feasibility reason, that control's accessible description (aria-describedby) must include the reason text currently shown on screen.

findings.theme: the hover highlight paints distance-ring styling that disagrees with the graph's actual hop distances
findings.summary: The second-ring set is built as "everything within 2 hops except the focus" instead of "exactly 2 hops", so it contains the first ring and `edgeClass` styles first-ring edges as second-ring edges.
findings.failure: Render GraphCanvas with the real core output `buildBuddyGraph(5, 4, {seed:12345})` (n=k+1 => K5, girth 3, m=10) and `hovered={0}`. Node classes are `[node sel, node hi, node hi, node hi, node hi]` — no `hi2`, correctly, since every other person is a direct buddy — but edge classes are `[edge lit x4, edge lit2 x6]`. `.edge.lit2` is `--cool2` at 0.4 opacity, the same token as `.node.hi2`, so six edges are painted as second-ring connections in a graph with no second ring. Restoring the `&& !f.has(c)` exclusion yields `[edge lit x4, edge dim x6]`. Reproduced via renderToStaticMarkup; the same happens for any focus inside a triangle (also reachable from any imported girth-3 file). All 135 existing tests pass with the defect present — nothing in app/test references `hi2`, `lit2`, or the highlight sets.
findings.remediation: Make the ring sets disjoint AT CONSTRUCTION rather than relying on check order: build `second` as strictly distance-2 (`if (c !== focus && !first.has(c)) s.add(c)`), or better, derive both rings from one pass that assigns each vertex its exact hop distance and buckets on it. Name the sibling: `nodeClass` currently only looks right because `first.has(i)` is tested before `second.has(i)`, so the same root cause is one reordering away from also corrupting node styling — fixing the set, not the consumer, closes both.
findings.invariant: For every graph and every focus vertex f, the highlight sets are exactly the BFS distance classes of f: first === {v : dist(f,v) === 1} and second === {v : dist(f,v) === 2}. Consequently first ∩ second === ∅, f ∉ first ∪ second, and no edge whose endpoints are both at distance <= 1 from f may receive the second-ring class. Checkable as a property over arbitrary (n, edges, focus).

findings.theme: The core `Graph` reconstruction from a `GraphView`'s flat edge list — needed by any per-node graph query (F8's eccentricity-per-node, F10's shortest-path) — currently lives inlined inside file-import validation rather than as a reusable, GraphView-scoped adapter.
findings.summary: `importGraph` is the ONLY place in app/src that turns a flat `[number,number][]` edge list back into a core `Graph` (lines 127-144: `new Graph(n)` + a loop of `g.addEdge`), and that loop is interleaved with import-only validation (edge-range checks, ImportError throws) in the same function. F8 (node explorer: eccentricity — 'at most N hops from anyone') and F10 (path finder) both need a `Graph` built from the CURRENT `GraphView.edges` (not a freshly-imported file) to call the core's `bfsDistances`/etc. on, and there is no shared, import-agnostic `graphFromView(view): Graph` today.
findings.failure: Building F8 or F10 today forces a choice: duplicate the `new Graph(n)`/`addEdge` loop in a new graph/explorer module (drifting from importGraph's version, e.g. its silent self-loop/dup-edge tolerance), or reach into `importGraph.ts` for a helper that was written and tested as an import-format validator, not a general adapter — coupling an explorer/path-finder to file-parsing code for an unrelated reason.
findings.invariant: Every code path in app/src that needs a core `Graph` for a given `GraphView` obtains it from one shared, side-effect-free function (not a copy of the addEdge loop and not by depending on io/importGraph.ts for a reason unrelated to importing a file).
findings.remediation: When F8 or F10 lands (the second caller that actually justifies it — extracting now would be premature per this repo's own YAGNI rule, since importGraph is presently the only caller), extract the `new Graph(n)`/addEdge loop out of importGraph.ts into a small `graph/fromView.ts` (or similar) that both importGraph and the new feature call, keeping importGraph's edge-shape validation local to importGraph.

findings.theme: F10 (path finder, PROJECT_PLAN.md M3, acceptance: 'path matches BFS; ties broken deterministically') needs an actual shortest-path (vertex sequence), but the only traversal primitive the core exports is `bfsDistances` (a distance vector, no predecessor/path) — so app/src currently has no way to satisfy F10 without either violating the stated 'no BFS/ASPL/Moore code in app/' boundary or adding new core surface.
findings.summary: `lib/src/core/index.ts` re-exports `bfsDistances`, `isConnected`, `allPairsSummary`, `girth`, `largestComponentFraction` — nothing that returns an actual path. Reconstructing a path from `bfsDistances` output would require walking backward from the target through neighbours with distance-1, choosing a tie-break — that reconstruction logic is itself graph-traversal code, which app/CLAUDE.md's architecture section says never belongs in app/ ('If a number is missing, add it to the core (lib-first), not here').
findings.failure: An engineer implementing F10 by calling `bfsDistances` from GraphCanvas/a new PathFinder panel and then hand-walking the distance array to reconstruct the path (to get the visible chain, not just its length) would be writing BFS-adjacent traversal code inside app/src, contradicting the explicit 'UI never reimplements math' / 'no BFS ... code in app/' architecture rule this same file states.
findings.invariant: For every feature acceptance criterion that names a specific graph-traversal RESULT (not just a scalar metric) — e.g. F10's actual shortest-chain vertex sequence with a deterministic tie-break — a core function returning exactly that result exists and app/src only calls it, never reconstructs it from a lower-level primitive.
findings.remediation: Lib-first: add a `shortestPath(g, u, v): number[] | null` (or similar) to lib/src/core with its own deterministic tie-break contract and tests, then have F10's app code call it — do not build this in app/src, and do not add it to the core now (no caller yet) purely to pre-harden the seam.

findings.theme: Control character regex definitions duplicated across modules
findings.summary: The regex pattern for detecting control characters is defined identically in two modules but without a link between them, creating a maintenance burden and risk of silent drift.
findings.failure: If a maintainer changes one regex to support additional dangerous characters (e.g., to address a newly discovered spreadsheet formula injection vector) without updating the other, the two modules would have inconsistent behavior: parseRoster would normalize one set of characters while importGraph would reject a different set. Names could then survive import but get mangled on roster edit, violating the round-trip invariant.
findings.remediation: Extract the character class `[�-]` to a shared constant in a common module (e.g., `src/io/controlChars.ts: export const CONTROL_CHAR_CLASS = '[�-]'`), then build both regexes from it. Alternatively, add a targeted comment in both files that explicitly names the other location (e.g., '// Keep in sync with parseRoster.ts:20') so a contributor searching for uses of this pattern finds both.

findings.theme: the roster-setup dialog claims aria-modal but nothing enforces modality for keyboard/AT users — focus is never moved into it, background controls stay reachable while it is open, and focus is never restored when it closes
findings.summary: RosterModal renders `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` (App.tsx:165-173) but no code anywhere in the app moves DOM focus into it on open, traps Tab within it while open, or marks background content inert/aria-hidden. Reproduced by rendering App, generating a graph, clicking "Edit people" (App.tsx:153), and inspecting the DOM: `document.activeElement` stays on the (now visually covered, z-index-20-overlay-obscured) "Edit people" button — `dialog.contains(document.activeElement)` is false — and every background control (e.g. the "↻ Different arrangement" reroll button) remains present, not disabled, has no aria-hidden/inert ancestor, and is directly `.focus()`-able while the dialog is open.
findings.failure: Open "Edit people" from a full graph state, then press Tab repeatedly: instead of landing on the dialog's textarea (the visible next control), focus walks through roughly a dozen invisible-behind-the-overlay controls first — LayoutToggle's Ring/Force buttons, BuddyList's Copy/CSV/every person row, QualityPanel's Import/Print/Export buttons — before ever reaching the dialog content. A screen-reader user hears these fully-normal control announcements with no indication they belong to a hidden background, and activating one (e.g. Enter on the reroll button) silently regenerates the graph underneath the still-open "edit roster" dialog, leaving the dialog showing stale roster text over a graph that no longer matches it.
findings.remediation: On RosterModal mount, move focus to the dialog (e.g. the textarea or the dialog container with tabIndex={-1}), constrain Tab/Shift+Tab to the dialog's own focusable elements while it is open (a small focus-trap keydown handler, or the native <dialog>.showModal()), and mark the rest of #app inert (or aria-hidden="true" plus tabIndex=-1 on its focusable descendants) for the duration. The same treatment applies to the `.busy` generating-overlay in App.tsx:175-182, which has the identical gap.
findings.invariant: While any element with role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" is present in the DOM, every element outside that dialog's subtree must be excluded from the Tab sequence (aria-hidden or inert or tabIndex=-1), and the initial focus after the dialog mounts must be inside the dialog subtree.

findings.theme: the roster-setup dialog claims aria-modal but nothing enforces modality for keyboard/AT users — focus is never moved into it, background controls stay reachable while it is open, and focus is never restored when it closes
findings.summary: onCancel/onGenerate/applyImported all close RosterModal purely via `setModalOpen(false)` (App.tsx:65-66, 105, 171) with no focus bookkeeping. Reproduced: render App, generate a graph, open "Edit people", focus and click the dialog's "Cancel" button, then inspect `document.activeElement` — it is `<body>` (`document.activeElement === document.body` is true). The same happens on the initial "Generate buddy graph" click, since handleGenerate also unmounts the modal without any focus target, and on the error-recovery reopen (bg.status==="error" && !view -> setModalOpen(true) in the effect at App.tsx:41-51), which likewise never focuses the reopened dialog.
findings.failure: A screen-reader user who presses Cancel (or Generate, or completes an import) has their focus silently dropped to <body>. The next Tab press restarts keyboard navigation from the very top of the document (past the header, brand, privacy notice) instead of continuing near the control they just used — on every single roster-setup interaction, including the error-recovery path the scenario specifically calls out ("recover from an error along the way").
findings.remediation: Track the element that had focus before the dialog opened (or the specific trigger button, e.g. "Edit people"/"Generate buddy graph") and restore focus to it explicitly when the dialog closes, for every close path (Cancel, successful Generate, successful Import). For the reactive error-recovery reopen, move focus into the reopened dialog rather than leaving it wherever it happened to be.
findings.invariant: For every open/close cycle of the role="dialog" element, document.activeElement after close must be a still-mounted, non-body element (ideally the element that had focus, or was clicked to open the dialog, immediately before open) — it must never equal document.body.

findings.theme: a persistent selection toggle changes app state and view highlighting but exposes no ARIA state for it
findings.summary: Each buddy-list row is a `<button className={"brow" + (selected === i ? " sel" : "")}>` (BuddyList.tsx:49-56) that calls `onSelect(i)` — the sole keyboard path to selecting a person and lighting up their buddies in the graph (per GraphCanvas.tsx:207-213's own comment, the graph is intentionally non-interactive for keyboard users and BuddyList is the accessible substitute). The selected/unselected distinction is expressed only via the `sel` CSS class; the button has no `aria-pressed` or `aria-current` attribute, unlike LayoutToggle's buttons which correctly set `aria-pressed={layout === m}` (LayoutToggle.tsx:15) for the analogous pattern.
findings.failure: A screen-reader user tabs to a row and presses Enter/Space to "select" that person (the documented way to highlight their buddies in the graph view). Because every row already shows its buddies as static text regardless of selection, nothing in the announcement changes after activating the button, so the user has no accessible confirmation the keypress registered, and cannot query which row is presently selected without re-deriving it visually.
findings.remediation: Add `aria-pressed={selected === i}` (matching LayoutToggle's existing pattern) or `aria-current={selected === i ? "true" : undefined}` to each `.brow` button in BuddyList.tsx.
findings.invariant: For every row i in the buddy list, the DOM aria-pressed/aria-current value on that row's button must equal (selected === i), immediately after any selection change.

findings.theme: the hover highlight tells the user something the graph does not draw: second-degree buddies are computed and used to light EDGES but are rendered as unrelated NODES, so the picture contradicts itself
findings.summary: `nodeClass`'s `second.has(i)` branch returns "node faded" — byte-identical to the fall-through "unrelated" branch — so the 2-hop neighbour set has zero effect on node rendering while `edgeClass` still returns "edge lit2" for the same ring. `.node.hi2` in app.css becomes unreachable, and because `.node text` has `opacity: 0` unless hi/sel/hi2, a second-ring person's NAME is not shown at all. The mock (mock/app.js:186, the design source of truth) does `else if(second.has(i))g.classList.add('hi2')`, and the app's edgeClass still matches the mock exactly, so nodeClass is the sole deviation.
findings.failure: SSR-render GraphCanvas with names=[A,B,C,D], edges=[[0,1],[1,2],[2,3]], adjacency=[[1],[0,2],[1,3],[2]], layout="ring", hovered=0. Actual node classes: ['node sel','node hi','node faded','node faded']; edge classes: ['edge lit','edge lit2','edge lit2']. Vertex 2 is a genuine second-degree buddy yet gets the same class as unrelated vertex 3 (dot opacity 0.22, label opacity 0), while the edge 1-2 that reaches it is drawn highlighted (.edge.lit2, stroke-opacity 0.4, --cool2). Expected 'node hi2'. Reproduced; the existing suite is green (147 tests) and `npm run lint` at the repo root is clean, because no test asserts any hover class (graphCanvas.smoke.test.tsx counts elements only; graphCanvasDefer.test.tsx passes hovered={null}) and the hygiene dead-CSS check matches \bhi2\b against mock/app.js, which still contains it.
findings.remediation: Restore `if (second.has(i)) return "node hi2";` in nodeClass. Then close the two gaps that let it through: (1) add a GraphCanvas render test that, for a fixed graph and a fixed focus, asserts the four hover-ring memberships (focus / first / second / neither) map to four PAIRWISE-DISTINCT node class strings and that every class returned has a matching rule in app.css; (2) make the hygiene dead-CSS-hook check scan app/src (and lib) separately from mock/, so a hook kept alive only by the unwired prototype still reports as dead.
findings.invariant: For every adjacency list and every focus vertex f, `nodeClass` is INJECTIVE over hover-ring membership: the class strings returned for f itself, for a first-degree neighbour, for a second-degree neighbour, and for a vertex in none of those are pairwise distinct. Corollary that must also hold for all inputs: no vertex incident to an edge classed "edge lit2" may carry the same node class as a vertex all of whose edges are classed "edge dim"; and every class string nodeClass can return has a matching selector in app/src/styles/app.css.

findings.theme: the next committed feature (F10 path finder) needs a shortest-PATH (vertex sequence), but the core only exposes shortest-DISTANCE
findings.summary: lib/src/core/metrics.ts exports bfsDistances(g, s) → Int32Array of distances only; there is no predecessor-tracking / path-reconstructing BFS anywhere in lib/src/core (confirmed by grep across lib/src/core/*.ts and reference-python/*.py — neither has one). F10's acceptance criteria ('path matches BFS; ties broken deterministically') require an actual vertex sequence, not just a distance vector. Per app/CLAUDE.md's architecture rule ('The UI never reimplements math... No BFS/ASPL/Moore code in app/'), the correct fix is lib-first, but no such function currently exists and nothing in the current tree calls one — so per this lens's hard rule this is filed as a deferral, not blocking/suggestion, even though it is a real gap surfaced by attempting the actual next committed change (not an invented feature).
findings.failure: Implementing F10 today without a lib addition forces one of two violations: (a) reimplement BFS-with-predecessors in app/src (breaks the 'UI never reimplements math' rule that already holds cleanly for every other metric), or (b) call bfsDistances repeatedly / walk distances greedily in the UI to fake a path, which does not guarantee the same deterministic tie-break the core's own traversal order would produce (adjacency order lives in Graph.adj, which the UI does not see in a form suited to path walking).
findings.remediation: When F10 is actually started, add a path-reconstructing BFS (e.g. bfsPath(g, s, t): number[] | null, or expose predecessors from bfsDistances) to lib/src/core/metrics.ts first, validate its tie-break against reference-python (or document that the Python oracle doesn't cover it and add a property test instead), then have the app call it — mirroring how every other metric (aspl, girth, allPairsSummary) is already lib-first.
findings.invariant: For every displayed graph-derived value (including a highlighted path), there exists a corresponding pure function exported from lib/src/core that produces it; app/src contains no BFS/shortest-path traversal loop of its own. Mechanical check: grep app/src for adjacency-walking loops that compute reachability/distance/path outside of a call into `ringweave`.

findings.theme: the app's one selection primitive (`selected: number | null`) and its one click handler are wired for exactly one meaning (row/node focus for hover-glow), with no seam for a second concurrent selection kind or for keyboard-cancel
findings.summary: `selected`/`onSelect` is a single `number | null` threaded through App.tsx, GraphCanvas.tsx (node click → onSelect(i), background click → onSelect(null), drives the hover/select neighborhood glow via `focus = hovered ?? selected` at GraphCanvas.tsx:177), and BuddyList.tsx (row click → onSelect(i), drives the `sel` row class). F10 needs a two-endpoint pick ('select two people') that is a materially different interaction and a materially different highlight (a path overlay, not a 1st/2nd-order neighborhood glow) layered on the same click surfaces. There is also no keydown/Escape handling anywhere in app/src (grep confirms zero matches for `keydown`/`Escape`), so F10's 'ESC clears' acceptance criterion has no existing hook — it requires a new global listener, most naturally added at the App.tsx composition root.
findings.failure: Implementing F10 by literally reusing today's `selected`/`onSelect(i)` would collapse 'pick path endpoint A' into the same call as 'select this row/node for hover-glow', so clicking a second person to set path endpoint B would also silently reassign the ordinary single-selection focus (or vice versa) unless the click handler is given new mode-aware branching in all three files — a real fan-out across App.tsx (new state + mode-aware handler + new keydown listener), GraphCanvas.tsx (nodeClass/edgeClass would need a third highlight tier, precedence undefined against the existing sel/hi/faded scheme), and BuddyList.tsx (row click semantics diverge by mode). None of this is wrong in the code as it stands today (M2 has no path-picking requirement), but it means F10 cannot land as a single-file or single-seam change the way, say, a new tag policy would in the core.
findings.remediation: Before starting F10, design the interaction as a distinct mode (e.g. `pickMode: 'select' | 'path-from' | 'path-to'` or a separate `pathEndpoints: [number, number] | null` state) rather than overloading `selected`, and add the ESC listener once at the App.tsx composition root feeding a single 'clear transient UI state' function (the existing `resetSelection` pattern is a reasonable base to extend). Decide highlight precedence (hover glow vs. path overlay) once, in one place, rather than layering ad hoc class strings in GraphCanvas.
findings.invariant: Selecting a path endpoint never mutates the plain hover/select focus used for BuddyList row highlighting, and vice versa: for all sequences of clicks, `selected` (single-focus) and the path endpoints (if introduced) are independently readable and independently clearable. Mechanical check once built: a click that sets a path endpoint does not change GraphCanvas's `nodeClass`/`edgeClass` output for the unrelated single-select focus.

findings.theme: Parameter name drifts from established vocabulary, creating confusion about what value should be passed
findings.summary: The `k` parameter in quality() is misleadingly named; it should be `maxDegree` or `actualDegree`
findings.failure: Developer calls quality(aspl, n, settings.buddies) for an irregular graph where degreeMax ≠ buddies, producing wrong score. Test at line 105 of importExport.roundtrip.test.ts shows this risk: 'scored at k=2, not 4' where k=2 is degreeMax and 4 is the declared target buddies.
findings.invariant: The k parameter to quality() must always be the actual maximum degree of the graph (raw.degreeMax in assembleMetrics), never the target buddy count (settings.buddies). For regular graphs these are equal so the confusion is silent; for irregular graphs (odd n×k) they differ and using the wrong value produces incorrect quality scores.
findings.remediation: Rename the parameter from `k` to `maxDegree` (or `actualDegree`), and add a docstring: 'quality(aspl: number, n: number, maxDegree: number): number — returns the Moore-gap quality score. Note: maxDegree is the actual graph degree, not the target buddy count; for generated graphs, assembleMetrics passes raw.degreeMax.'

findings.theme: role=dialog/aria-modal claims a modality the DOM does not enforce, and no code ever moves focus
findings.summary: RosterModal renders `<div id="modal" role="dialog" aria-modal="true">` but nothing in the component (or App.tsx) ever calls `.focus()`, sets `autoFocus`, or restores focus on close. A whole-tree grep for `.focus(`/`autoFocus`/`tabIndex` across app/src returns zero hits outside the hidden file-input refs, so this is not a coverage gap in one path — no dialog in the app manages focus at all.
findings.failure: Keyboard/screen-reader walkthrough: on cold load `modalOpen` starts true and the dialog is the only content, so it happens to work by accident. But click "Edit people" (App.tsx:153) while a graph is showing: `setModalOpen(true)` mounts RosterModal *after* the still-rendered stage/rail/LayoutToggle/BuddyList/QualityPanel in DOM order (App.tsx:132-173), while focus stays on the "Edit people" button the user just activated — which is now visually behind the modal overlay (`#modal` is only `position:absolute; z-index:20`, app.css:140, no `inert`/`aria-hidden` is ever applied to the background). Pressing Tab or Shift+Tab, or browsing with a screen reader's virtual cursor, reaches LayoutToggle/BuddyList rows/QualityPanel's Import/Print/Export buttons — all still focusable and operable underneath a dialog that claims aria-modal="true". Conversely, closing the dialog (Cancel at RosterModal.tsx:103, or Generate at :104-106 unmounting via App.tsx onGenerate/onCancel) removes the currently-focused element from the DOM with nothing to receive focus, so the browser default drops focus to <body> — the next Tab press restarts keyboard navigation from the top of the page instead of returning to "Edit people"/wherever the user came from. Same story for the busy overlay's Cancel button (App.tsx:179) and for a first-generation error reopening the modal (App.tsx:41-51): focus is never placed into it, so a screen-reader user who is told "Generation failed" via the toast has no cue their next Tab lands inside a freshly-reopened setup dialog rather than continuing where they were.
findings.invariant: When an element with role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" mounts, focus must move to an element inside it (and Tab/Shift+Tab must not be able to move focus outside it while it remains mounted); when it unmounts, focus must move to a specific, sane element (typically the control that opened it) — never fall through to document.body.
findings.remediation: On mount, focus the first sensible control (e.g. the textarea) with a ref + useEffect; trap Tab within the dialog (a small focus-trap effect, or FocusTrap/`<dialog>` element with `showModal()` which gets trap-and-restore for free); on close, focus the element that had focus before the dialog opened (store it in a ref on open). Add `aria-hidden`/`inert` to `#app`'s main content while the modal is open as a second line of defense so a screen reader's linear/virtual-cursor browsing also can't reach it.

findings.theme: validation/error text that appears and disappears in the DOM is never wrapped in a live region, so a screen-reader user gets no announcement of refusals
findings.summary: Grepping RosterModal.tsx and SettingsControls.tsx for aria-live/role="alert"/role="status" returns nothing. `fileError` (a rejected/oversized file drop, io/readFileText.ts errors), `inputCapped` (huge paste truncation), `parsed.warnings` (duplicate-name notices from parseRoster), and `feas.messages` (the "blocking" infeasible-settings gate, e.g. changing the buddies-per-person stepper past what the roster supports) are each rendered as plain `<div className="note">`/`<div className="note blocking">` (RosterModal.tsx:109-116) that mount/unmount/change text as the user types, drags a file, or adjusts SettingsControls — with no `aria-live` region, `role="alert"`, or `role="status"` anywhere to catch the change. This is a direct regression against the pattern the app itself documents as correct: Notice.tsx (the App-level toast) is explicitly built with a persistently-mounted `role="status"` region "so assistive tech announces a content change in a region it is already watching" (Notice.tsx:9-11) — that reasoning was never applied to RosterModal's own inline notes.
findings.failure: Scenario from the task: drag-drop a .csv that readFileText rejects (e.g. wrong extension or over the read size cap) — `fileError` is set (RosterModal.tsx:53-55) and a `<div className="note blocking">` appears with the message. A screen-reader user who dropped the file (or clicked "choose a file") gets zero announcement; they must manually re-navigate the dialog to discover the note exists. Same for the more common case in the scenario's own script — "find one specific person" implies configuring settings first: nudging the "Buddies each" stepper (SettingsControls.tsx:30-33, plain +/- buttons) into an infeasible value for the roster size flips `feas.canGenerate` to false, silently disabling "Generate buddy graph" (RosterModal.tsx:104) and printing the reason in an unannounced note — the user hears nothing explaining why the button they just tabbed to is now unavailable.
