findings.invariant: Every DOM node that conditionally renders user-facing validation/error/warning text (appears, disappears, or changes content in response to user input) is either inside a persistently-mounted `aria-live`/`role="status"` region, or uses `role="alert"` for the blocking cases — so the message is announced without requiring the user to relocate focus to discover it.
findings.remediation: Wrap the notes container in a persistently-mounted `<div aria-live="polite">` (or `role="status"`) matching Notice.tsx's own pattern; use `role="alert"`/`aria-live="assertive"` for the `blocking` class specifically since it gates the primary action. Additionally, `aria-describedby` the disabled "Generate buddy graph" button to the blocking feasibility message id so a screen reader announces the reason at the moment the button itself receives focus, not only if the live region happened to fire earlier.

findings.theme: a control's selected/active state is expressed only via a CSS class, invisible to the accessibility tree
findings.summary: Each buddy-list row is a real `<button>` (good — reachable and operable) but its selected state is expressed only as `className={"brow" + (selected === i ? " sel" : "")}` (BuddyList.tsx:51) with no `aria-pressed`/`aria-current`/`aria-selected` counterpart. This is the exact class of gap the a11y linter cannot catch (an absent attribute, not a misused one), and the app itself demonstrates the correct pattern one file away: LayoutToggle.tsx:15 sets `aria-pressed={layout === m}` specifically "to expose the active mode to assistive tech, not just via CSS" — that reasoning was never carried over to BuddyList's row selection, which is the scenario's actual "find one specific person, discover who their buddies are" interaction.
findings.failure: Keyboard/screen-reader walkthrough of the scenario: Tab into the Buddy list (BuddyList.tsx:39, aria-label="Buddy list"), Tab/arrow through the row buttons to "Alice Nguyen", press Enter/Space to select her — `onSelect(i)` fires and the row visually highlights (`.sel` class) and the graph glows her buddies via `nodeClass`/`edgeClass` in GraphCanvas (which is explicitly documented as a non-keyboard-reachable view, delegating state to this list). A screen reader announces only "Alice Nguyen, button" both before and after activation — there is no accessible confirmation that the selection took effect, and re-visiting the row list later gives no way to tell which row (if any) is currently selected without re-triggering it, unlike a sighted user who sees the `.sel` background.
findings.invariant: Every interactive control whose selected/active state is expressed via a CSS class must expose an equivalent ARIA state attribute (aria-pressed for a toggle button, aria-current for a "currently viewed item" in a list) that is present and correct on every render where the class is present, mirroring the class 1:1.
findings.remediation: Add `aria-pressed={selected === i}` (or `aria-current={selected === i ? "true" : undefined}`, whichever semantic fits "currently selected person in a list" better) to the row button in BuddyList.tsx alongside the existing `sel` class, matching the pattern already used in LayoutToggle.tsx.

findings.theme: the graph view highlights the wrong edges, so the visual contradicts the graph the core returned and the hover affordance the UI advertises
findings.summary: `edgeClass` negates the second-ring predicate, so edges far from the focus render highlighted (`lit2`) and the genuine two-hop edges render suppressed (`dim`) — the exact complement of the intended (and mock-specified) classification.
findings.failure: Render GraphCanvas with C10 (names P0..P9, edges [i,(i+1)%10]), layout="ring", selected=0. Actual line classes in order: lit, dim, dim, lit2, lit2, lit2, lit2, dim, dim, lit. Expected (mock/app.js:167): lit, lit2, lit2, dim, dim, dim, dim, lit2, lit2, lit. Node classes are correct (0 sel, 1/9 hi, 2/8 hi2, 3-7 faded), so hovering P0 dims the edges around its own hi2 neighbours and lights up the band on the opposite side of the ring — directly contradicting the on-screen hint "Hover a person to light their buddies". `npm test` passes 135/135; no test in app/test/ asserts any edge class, so the whole class of defect is unwatched.
findings.remediation: Restore the positive predicate: `if (second.has(u) || second.has(v)) return "edge lit2"; return "edge dim";`. Close the theme, not the line: export the classifier (or assert on rendered `line`/`g.node` classes) and add a test that ties BOTH edge and node classes to BFS distance from the focus for an arbitrary graph, so any future re-derivation of either predicate is caught.
findings.invariant: For every graph, every focus f, and every edge (u,v): the emitted class is `lit` iff u===f||v===f; otherwise it is `lit2` iff min(dist(f,u),dist(f,v))===2 and `dim` iff min(dist(f,u),dist(f,v))>=3. Equivalently and mechanically: no edge with both endpoints at BFS distance >=3 from f may carry a highlight class, and no edge with an endpoint at distance exactly 2 from f may carry `dim`. (Holds for all n, all edge sets, and every focus.)

findings.theme: the roster/settings the UI acts on can diverge from the roster/settings of the graph it is displaying, so a button silently operates on people who are not on screen
findings.summary: `handleGenerate` commits `names`/`settings` before the worker result arrives, and `handleReroll` rerolls from that state instead of `view.names`/`view.settings` — so after a cancelled or failed generation, "Different arrangement" replaces the displayed group with a different roster.
findings.failure:
With the worker hook mocked (as in test/appErrorRecovery.test.tsx): generate roster A = "A
B
C
D
E" and deliver a done result (rail shows `5`); click "Edit people", set the textarea to 8 names, click "Generate buddy graph" (status running); click "Cancel" in the busy overlay (reset -> idle, view is still the 5-person graph, rail still shows `5`); click "↻ Different arrangement". Observed dispatch: {"n":8,"k":4,"options":{"polish":"auto","seed":12346}} — the displayed 5-person graph is replaced by an 8-person graph the user never accepted. The same state is reached without cancelling when generation errors (view kept, names already swapped). Consequences share the root cause: the reroll gates `feasibility(names.length, …)` and `rerollBlockReason(names.length, …)` judge the abandoned roster (a cancelled 500-person generate makes reroll on a displayed 10-person graph refuse with "too large to shuffle"), and the Advanced panel/`initialText` show the abandoned roster's settings/text.
findings.remediation: Derive the reroll's inputs from the displayed graph, not from pending UI state: in `handleReroll` use `view.names` and `{...view.settings, seed: nextRerollSeed(view.settings.seed)}` (and gate on `view.names.length`). Better by subtraction: stop keeping `names`/`settings` as App state that is written before the result lands — treat `view` as the single source for both, and let RosterModal own only its own draft text. Ratchet with an App-level test covering both non-adopting outcomes (cancel and error), since a fix for cancel alone leaves the error sibling open.
findings.invariant: Whenever `view !== null`, every reroll dispatch satisfies: the roster passed to the worker equals `view.names` (same length and same elements in order), and the settings passed equal `view.settings` except for `seed`, which equals `nextRerollSeed(view.settings.seed)`. Holds for all rosters, all settings, and all interleavings of generate/cancel/error/import.

findings.theme: GraphCanvas's node/edge highlight classification is a single mutually-exclusive state machine keyed on one `focus` variable, not a composable set of independent highlight sources — the next committed feature that needs a second, simultaneously-active highlight source has no seam to plug into.
findings.summary: `focus = hovered ?? selected` (line 177) feeds `nodeClass`/`edgeClass` (lines 192-205), which branch exhaustively and mutually-exclusively on that single value (`sel`/`hi`/`hi2`/`faded`, or the equivalent edge classes). F10 (path finder, PROJECT_PLAN.md §4 F10, committed M3/P1) requires highlighting a shortest buddy-chain — a second highlight source that must be visible independently of (and simultaneously with) the existing hover/select glow (e.g. a user can still hover a third node while a path is pinned). There is no accumulation mechanism (no class-list building from independent predicates); the two branches to add (`onPath(i)`, `pathEdge(u,v)`) cannot be layered onto the existing `if/else` chain without editing its existing branches, because each existing branch already returns a single terminal class string covering every case.
findings.failure: Concretely: implement F10 by adding a `path: number[] | null` prop and try to make a path-highlighted node also show the existing hover-glow `hi`/`hi2` styling when the user hovers a third node while a path is pinned — this requires rewriting nodeClass/edgeClass's branching (turning single-value `if/else` into class-list composition), not adding a new case to an existing switch the way `positionsFor`'s `assertNever` pattern allows for LayoutMode.
findings.remediation: Before F10 lands, refactor nodeClass/edgeClass into independent, composable predicates (e.g. build a Set<string> of classes from separate `isFocusSel`, `isFocusHi`, `isOnPath`, `isPathEndpoint` checks) so a second highlight source is additive rather than requiring a rewrite of the existing conditional.
findings.invariant: Adding a new independently-triggerable highlight source (e.g. `path`) must not require modifying the existing branches of nodeClass/edgeClass for the pre-existing hover/select source — today it does, since both are single-value exhaustive `if/else` chains with no class-list accumulation.

findings.theme: First/second-order neighbor computation (a 2-hop adjacency walk) exists only as a private, unexported closure inside the rendering component that happens to need it for hover, with no reusable form for the next feature that needs the identical computation.
findings.summary: Lines 178-188 compute `first`/`second` order neighbor sets from `adjacency` inside a `useMemo` local to GraphCanvas, keyed off the hover/select `focus`. F8 (node explorer, PROJECT_PLAN.md §4 F8, committed M3/P1) requires a panel showing "buddies (1st), reachable-in-2 (2nd), eccentricity" for an explicitly clicked/explored node — the exact same first/second-order computation, but driven by explorer state independent of canvas hover/select (the explorer panel must work even when nothing is hovered on the canvas, per the app's own "graph is a view, never the only interface" rule in app/CLAUDE.md). As written this logic is not exported and not reusable outside GraphCanvas, so building F8 either duplicates it in a second location or requires extracting it first — neither of which the current structure does for you.
findings.failure: Implement F8's explorer panel: it needs first/second-order sets for a node selected purely from the panel (no canvas hover), so it cannot call GraphCanvas's local `first`/`second` memo — the only path today is copy-pasting the same two-line set-walk into a new module, which is the exact duplication the codebase's own DRY/Clean-Code bar (lib/CLAUDE.md's quality bar, mirrored for app) is meant to prevent.
findings.remediation: Extract the first/second-order neighbor walk into a small exported helper (e.g. `src/graph/neighborhoods.ts`, `neighborsAtDistance(adjacency, i): {first: Set<number>, second: Set<number>}`) before F8 lands, and have GraphCanvas's hover-glow consume it — one implementation, two callers.
findings.invariant: The first/second-order neighbor computation should exist in exactly one exported location with N callers; today it exists in exactly one *unexported* location with exactly one caller, so a second caller (F8) cannot be added without duplicating or first extracting it.

findings.theme: App.tsx mixes an established hook-extraction pattern for heavy concerns (generation via useBuddyGraph, toasts via useNotice) with raw inline useState for other cross-cutting concerns (selection/hover), and the three next committed features each add their own new cross-cutting state with no established place to put it, risking App.tsx becoming a god component.
findings.summary: `selected`/`hovered` (lines 36-37) are raw `useState` in App.tsx, unlike `bg` (useBuddyGraph) and notice (useNotice), which are extracted hooks. F7 (constraint editing state), F8 (search query + explorer back-stack), and F10 (path start/end + pinned-path state) are each new cross-cutting state that, following the established *inconsistent* pattern, would most likely also land as raw useState directly in App.tsx alongside the existing ~10 pieces of state and ~8 handler functions it already owns (generate/reroll/import/export/cancel/resetSelection), compounding its responsibility count.
findings.failure: No single reproduction — this is a structural risk assessment, not a present defect: App.tsx today (204 lines, 8 pieces of state, 8 handlers) is still legible; three more features each adding 2-4 pieces of state and several handlers without hook extraction would push it toward the point where a single file owns roster lifecycle, generation orchestration, selection, search, exploration history, and path-picking simultaneously.
findings.remediation: When implementing F7/F8/F10, extract each feature's state machine into its own hook (e.g. `usePathFinder`, `useExplorer`, `useConstraintsEditor`) following the `useBuddyGraph`/`useNotice` precedent already in the codebase, rather than adding more raw useState calls to App.tsx.
findings.invariant: Cannot state a mechanical invariant for this one — it is a trend-based structural concern, not a property violated by a specific input today.

findings.theme: closing an overlay/replacing the graph never moves focus anywhere meaningful, so a keyboard/screen-reader user's place in the app is silently discarded
findings.summary: RosterModal has no focus management at all (no autoFocus into it on open, no focus restoration on close). When the modal closes — via Generate (line 65 `setModalOpen(false)` in handleGenerate), Cancel (`onCancel`), or a successful import (`applyImported`, line 105) — the previously-focused element (inside the now-unmounted dialog) is removed from the DOM, and neither React nor any effect calls .focus() on a replacement. The browser's default behavior is to move focus to document.body.
findings.failure: Reproduced directly: render App, type a roster into the textarea, focus the "Generate buddy graph" button, click it. `document.activeElement === document.body` is true immediately after — a screen-reader user who just generated a graph is dropped at the top of an unlabelled document with zero indication the new rail/graph/buddy-list/quality panel exist, let alone where they are. The same class of loss happens on Cancel and on a successful import.
findings.remediation: On every RosterModal-closing transition, move focus explicitly to a stable, meaningful anchor — e.g. the h1 (with tabIndex={-1}) or the rail's first control ("Different arrangement") after generate/import, and back to the triggering "Edit people"/"Import" button on Cancel — via a ref set in the same effect/handler that flips modalOpen.
findings.invariant: After any state transition that unmounts the currently-focused element, document.activeElement must be a visible, labelled element that is part of the newly-rendered content or the control that triggered the transition — never document.body.

findings.theme: the setup dialog is marked role=dialog/aria-modal=true but nothing actually constrains focus to it, so Tab reaches controls the user cannot see
findings.summary: App.tsx mounts the graph view (`{view && (...)}`, lines 132-163: rail buttons, LayoutToggle, BuddyList rows, QualityPanel buttons) unconditionally, and RosterModal (lines 165-173) is a DOM sibling that appears AFTER it, purely CSS-overlaid (`#modal { position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 20; ... }` in app.css) with no `inert`, no aria-hidden on the background, and no keydown-based focus trap in RosterModal.tsx. `aria-modal="true"` (line 69) asserts a guarantee the markup does not provide.
findings.failure: Reproduced directly: generate a graph, then click "Edit people" to reopen the setup modal over the live view. Walking document.querySelectorAll of all natively-focusable elements in DOM order and finding the dialog's position shows 14 background controls ahead of it: "↻ Different arrangement", "Edit people", both LayoutToggle buttons, Copy, CSV, all 5 buddy-list rows, and Import/Print/Export. A keyboard user tabbing forward from "Edit people" (the element that still has focus, since nothing moved it — see the companion focus-lost finding) lands on LayoutToggle's "Ring" button, then walks the entire buddy list and quality panel, all invisible behind the modal backdrop, before ever reaching the dialog's own textarea/settings/Generate button. Shift+Tab from inside the dialog leaks the same way in reverse.
findings.remediation: Either mark the background subtree `inert` (or `aria-hidden="true"` plus `tabIndex={-1}` on each control) whenever modalOpen is true, or implement a real focus trap in RosterModal (wrap-around Tab/Shift+Tab handling scoped to the dialog's own focusable set), and set initial focus into the dialog on open.
findings.invariant: While an element with role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" is present in the DOM, the ordered set of elements reachable by Tab/Shift+Tab from any starting point in the document must be a subset of that dialog's descendants.

findings.theme: dynamically appearing status/error text has no pre-existing live region to be announced through, so a screen-reader user only discovers it by later navigating to it
findings.summary: The "Generating…" busy overlay (lines 175-182) is a plain `<div className="busy">` with no `role="status"`/`aria-live`/`aria-busy` anywhere in App.tsx (confirmed by grep — zero matches). Every generate/reroll transitions `bg.status` idle→running→done/error with no accessible announcement of either edge: a screen-reader user who presses "Different arrangement" hears nothing start and, when it finishes, hears nothing change (the graph, rail count, and quality numbers just silently update behind wherever focus already is — which, per the companion finding, is often already lost to document.body).
findings.failure: Confirmed by source inspection: `grep -n "role=\|aria-live\|aria-busy" App.tsx` returns no matches. A screen-reader user triggering a reroll on a large roster (the app explicitly warns >300 people can take tens of seconds, feasibility.ts LARGE_ROSTER) gets total silence for that whole duration and no cue that the result landed.
findings.remediation: Add a persistent role="status" region (mirroring Notice.tsx's already-mounted-region pattern) that announces "Generating…" on running and a short summary ("Done — N people, Q% connection quality") on done/error transitions.
findings.invariant: Every user-visible status-only text change reachable without a page reload must be reflected inside an element with role="status"/"alert" (or aria-live) that already exists in the DOM before the change fires, so assistive tech reliably announces it.

findings.theme: dynamically appearing status/error text has no pre-existing live region to be announced through, so a screen-reader user only discovers it by later navigating to it
findings.summary: The file-error, char-cap, duplicate-warning, and feasibility notes (lines 109-116: `.note`/`.note blocking` divs) are plain, non-live divs. They render/change in direct response to typing in the roster textarea, dropping/choosing a file, or adjusting the Buddies stepper (SettingsControls) — all of which leave focus on the textarea or stepper button, nowhere near the notes. None of `fileError`/`inputCapped`/`parsed.warnings`/`feas.messages` is wrapped in a role="status"/"alert" or aria-live region, so a screen-reader user who, say, lowers "Buddies each" to a value that now blocks generation (`feas.canGenerate` false, Generate button silently becomes disabled) is told nothing — they must guess to Tab/read forward to discover why Generate stopped working.
findings.failure: Confirmed by full source read of RosterModal.tsx (lines 100-116): the Generate button (line 104) gets `disabled={!feas.canGenerate}` in the same render that produces the blocking note below it, with no aria-live announcing the note or the disablement. This is exactly the "infeasible settings combination" error path called out in scope, and it dead-ends silently for a non-sighted user.
findings.remediation: Wrap the notes list in a single role="status" (or role="alert" for the blocking ones) container that is always mounted (empty when there's nothing to say), matching the pattern already used correctly in Notice.tsx.
findings.invariant: Every user-visible status-only text change reachable without a page reload must be reflected inside an element with role="status"/"alert" (or aria-live) that already exists in the DOM before the change fires, so assistive tech reliably announces it.

findings.theme: a control's selected/current state is shown only by a CSS class, with no accessible-tree equivalent
findings.summary: Each buddy-list row (`<button className={"brow" + (selected === i ? " sel" : "")}>`, lines 49-56) is a genuine toggle of which person is currently selected/highlighted in the graph, exactly the pattern LayoutToggle.tsx correctly exposes via `aria-pressed` two files over — but BuddyList's row buttons carry no `aria-current`/`aria-pressed`/`aria-selected` at all. A screen-reader user tabbing through the list has no way to tell which row (if any) is currently selected; the only signal is the visual `.sel` class.
findings.failure: Confirmed by source read: the `sel` class is the sole selection signal on lines 49-56; no aria attribute anywhere in the component reflects `selected === i`.
findings.remediation: Add `aria-current={selected === i ? "true" : undefined}` (or `aria-pressed`) to each row button, mirroring LayoutToggle.tsx's existing pattern.
findings.invariant: For any control whose selected/current state is shown via a CSS class, an aria-current/aria-pressed/aria-selected attribute must mirror that same boolean so its accessible value differs iff the underlying state differs.

findings.theme: the displayed connection-quality score is normalized by the user's own buddy-count setting, so a badly-connected graph can outscore a well-connected one on the same roster and be captioned "well-linked" / "already optimal"
findings.summary: `assembleMetrics` scores quality as the Moore gap at the graph's OWN `degreeMax`. Because the Moore bound for k=2 is exactly the cycle, every k=2 generation is a perfect score. The panel then simultaneously displays a huge hop count and a 100 gauge with the caption "everyone's well-linked", and `isOptimal` fires so a re-roll flashes "That's already an optimal arrangement — a re-roll can't improve it." `connectionSummary`'s own documented contract is that "a connected-but-poor graph says 'loosely linked'"; a 60-hop-diameter chain is precisely that case and it says the opposite. Reachable from the app's own generate path with two clicks of the "−" stepper (BUDDY_MIN = 2), no import needed.
findings.failure: Reproduced via viewFromResult on real buildBuddyGraph output.  n=20, buddies=2 -> aspl 5.26, diameter 10, qualityPercent 100, isOptimal true, connectionSummary "everyone's well-linked".  n=1000, buddies=2 -> aspl 250.25, diameter 500, gauge 100, isOptimal true, "everyone's well-linked"; the SAME roster at buddies=12 -> aspl 3.01, gauge 94. The app scores the graph whose average separation is 83x worse strictly HIGHER, and only the worse one is claimed optimal. At n=120 the same inversion holds: k=2 -> gauge 100, k=12 -> gauge 93 (aspl 2.03).
findings.remediation: Keep the Moore gap as the engineering score, but stop letting it alone drive user-facing claims. Either (a) score against a fixed reference degree (the target `k`/BUDDY range) rather than the graph's own degreeMax so the number is comparable across the stepper, or (b) gate `connectionSummary`'s "well-linked" branch and `isOptimal` on an absolute closeness term as well (e.g. the displayed aspl/diameter), so a chain can never read "well-linked". Note the current behaviour is enshrined by app/test/quality.test.ts and importExport.roundtrip.test.ts ("imports provably-optimal graphs at 100%"), so the existing suite would not catch this — those assertions need to move with the fix.
findings.invariant: For any two Metrics produced from the same roster size n, both connected: qualityPercent(A) > qualityPercent(B) implies A.aspl <= B.aspl (the displayed score must be non-increasing in the displayed average hops at fixed n). Equivalently: connectionSummary(m) must never contain "well-linked", and isOptimal(m) must never be true, for any m whose displayed aspl exceeds the aspl of another achievable graph on the same roster.

findings.theme: the pre-generation cost warning shown to the organizer is a function of roster size alone, while actual generation cost is dominated by whether auto-polish runs and by the buddy count — so the warning fires on fast configurations and is silent on the slowest one
findings.summary: `feasibility` emits its "large group — generating can take a while (tens of seconds near the limit)" note purely on `n > LARGE_ROSTER (300)`. But the core auto-enables the O(n·m)/iter polish pass only for n <= 120, so cost is non-monotone in n: the app's slowest reachable configuration sits just BELOW the warning threshold and is announced with nothing at all, while a large low-k roster that finishes in milliseconds gets the scary note. The organizer is told "that's fine" and then watches a ~40 s spinner.
findings.failure: Measured with node against lib/dist (buildBuddyGraph, default options):  n=120,k=12 -> 38,675 ms, and feasibility(120,12) returns {canGenerate:true, messages:[]} — no warning at all.  n=121,k=12 -> 141 ms (polish off).  n=1000,k=2 -> 105 ms, yet feasibility(301,2) already returns the "301 people is a large group … tens of seconds" note. So the note is a false negative at the measured worst case and a false positive at a case ~370x faster.
findings.remediation: Replace the bare `n > LARGE_ROSTER` predicate with the app's own cost estimate that includes k and whether auto-polish will run (n <= POLISH_MAX_N and polish !== false) — e.g. warn when the estimate exceeds a wall-clock budget, so both (120,12) and (1000,12) warn and (301,2) does not. Add a test pinning that the note fires for the polish-band worst corner.
findings.invariant: For every (n,k) pair the app can dispatch, let cost(n,k) be the app's generation-cost estimate. cost must be non-decreasing in n only when auto-polish state is held fixed, must be non-decreasing in k, and must account for the polish band; and the slow-generation note must fire iff cost exceeds the threshold. Consequently: there must exist NO pair A,B of dispatchable settings where feasibility warns for A, does not warn for B, and B's measured generation time exceeds A's.

findings.theme: the settings the app stores, displays and exports are not the settings it actually sent to the core
findings.summary: `generate` downgrades `polish: true` to `"auto"` whenever `names.length > POLISH_MAX_N` (a legitimate cost gate), but the downgrade is applied only to the dispatched options — `pending.current.settings` keeps `polish: true`, so `viewFromResult` stores it, the Advanced panel keeps showing "on", and `exportGraph` writes `settings.polish: true` into the file. Since "auto" is OFF above that n, the graph was generated unpolished while every surface claims polish ran. `BuddyResult.polished` is discarded by `viewFromResult`, so nothing in the app can detect the divergence. Unlike the reroll path (which at least flashes "too large to shuffle"), a plain Edit→Generate at n>120 with polish=on says nothing.
findings.failure: Trace: App.handleGenerate(roster of 500, {polish:true}) -> setSettings({polish:true}) and bg.generate(...). useBuddyGraph.generate computes polish = "auto" (500 > 120) and dispatches that; the core's resolveWantPolish("auto", 500) is false, so no polish runs. pending.settings still carries polish:true, so view.settings.polish === true. SettingsControls renders the select as "on" and exportGraph emits "polish": true for a graph that was never polished. (app/test/useBuddyGraph.test.tsx:232 asserts only the DISPATCHED value, never that the stored view.settings matches it — the gap is untested.)
findings.remediation: Make the downgrade the single source: compute the effective settings once, store THOSE in `pending.current.settings` (so the view/export/panel reflect what actually ran), and surface the downgrade to the user the way `rerollBlockReason` surfaces the reroll case. Longer term, plumb `BuddyResult.polished` into the view so the app reports measured rather than requested state.
findings.invariant: For every generation, the settings stored on the resulting GraphView (and therefore displayed by SettingsControls and written by exportGraph) must be field-for-field equal to the options actually dispatched to the core: view.settings.polish === dispatchedOptions.polish, view.settings.seed === dispatchedOptions.seed, view.settings.minSeparation === dispatchedOptions.minSeparation.

findings.theme: GraphCanvas's node/edge highlight classification has no extension point analogous to positionsFor, so the next two committed selection-driven features (F10 path highlight, F8 node-explorer reuse) can only be added by editing branch logic in place, hand-composing two independently-triggered highlight sources (hover-focus glow and a to-be-added path/explorer highlight) with no shared policy layer to reconcile them
findings.summary: `focus = hovered ?? selected` (line 177) feeds a single first/second neighbor-ring Set computation (178-188), consumed by `nodeClass`/`edgeClass` (192-205) — an un-exported, un-abstracted pair of functions with no policy indirection, no exhaustiveness guard, and only one caller. Contrast with `positionsFor` a few lines above, which is deliberately extracted, exported, tested (graphCanvasFit.test.ts), and protected by `assertNever` so a new LayoutMode fails to compile until handled. Highlighting has none of that: it is inline component logic keyed on one implicit 'focus' concept (single hovered-or-selected node, hop-distance rings).
findings.failure: F10 ("select two people, see the shortest buddy-chain highlighted", PROJECT_PLAN.md:119-121, M3) needs to render a specific ordered edge/vertex sequence between two chosen endpoints — a shape unrelated to hop-distance-from-one-focus. Implementing it means either (a) growing `nodeClass`/`edgeClass` with a third, orthogonal classification (path membership) reconciled ad hoc against the existing focus/first/second branches (what wins when a node is both `second`-order-from-hover and on the highlighted path?), or (b) duplicating the render loop. Neither is guided by any seam; unlike `positionsFor`, nothing forces an explicit, exhaustive decision — it is easy to ship a version where hover glow silently overrides or fights the path highlight.
findings.remediation: Before F10 lands, extract a single `classify(i)`/`classifyEdge(u,v)` policy that takes an explicit, prioritized list of active highlight sources (focus-ring, path) and produces one CSS class, mirroring the discipline already applied to `positionsFor` — so a second highlight mode is an added case, not a merge into existing conditionals.
findings.invariant: For any node i and any combination of {focus-hover active, path-highlight active}, exactly one deterministic class is produced by a single point of composition — not by two independently-evaluated conditionals whose precedence is decided by branch order in the render function.

findings.theme: The single selected/hovered state pair in App.tsx is dual-purposed (BuddyList row highlight + GraphCanvas single-focus glow) with no room for a second, independent selection concept, and F10's two-endpoint interaction is unaddressed by any existing prop or reset path
findings.summary: `selected`/`hovered` (App.tsx:36-37) are threaded into both `BuddyList` (row highlight + the only non-graph way to select) and `GraphCanvas` (focus glow), and cleared together by one `resetSelection()` (55-58) called from three graph-replacing call sites (handleGenerate, handleReroll, applyImported). F10 needs a *second*, independent selection concept — two chosen endpoints, distinct from 'the currently glowing person' — with its own reset lifecycle and its own non-graph (keyboard/panel) entry point per the NFR ('every operation works from the table/panel UI'). Nothing in App.tsx, BuddyList.tsx, or GraphCanvas.tsx's props reserves room for this; BuddyList's `onSelect: (i: number) => void` is a single click meaning 'focus/select this one person,' so a path-endpoint pick would have to be a new, disambiguated interaction (e.g. a separate button/panel), not a natural extension of the existing click handler.
findings.failure: Implementing F10 means adding parallel state (e.g. pathA/pathB) to App.tsx, a new prop pair to GraphCanvas, a new reset call added to the same three sites resetSelection already touches, and a new UI affordance (BuddyList's single-click-to-select semantics can't double as two-endpoint picking without a mode flag distinguishing 'select' from 'pick path endpoint' clicks) — none of which has a seam prepared, unlike layout mode.
findings.remediation: When F10 lands, generalize selection into one small state shape (e.g. `{ mode: 'select'|'path'; a: number|null; b: number|null }`) owned in one place (App.tsx or a small hook) rather than adding a second ad hoc pair of useState calls threaded independently through the same three components.
findings.invariant: Selecting or clearing a path endpoint never silently mutates the unrelated single-focus `selected` value used for the BuddyList row highlight, and vice versa.

findings.theme: Comment describes ring seed's effect on connectivity without clarifying that code assumes rather than verifies this property
findings.summary: Comment on viewFromResult misleads about connectivity verification
findings.failure: Line 244-245 says 'The unconstrained builder seeds a ring, so its output is always connected' but the code hardcodes connected:true without measurement. A maintainer would read this as: the core guarantees connectivity via the ring seed. The actual situation is that the code ASSUMES connectivity (it's not verified) because BuddyResult carries no connectivity field. The CLAUDE.md explicitly documents this: 'Generation connectivity is assumed, not measured... viewFromResult sets connected:true / largestComponentFraction:1 because BuddyResult carries no connectivity field and the ring seed guarantees connectivity by construction.' The comment's prose obscures that this is an assumption, not a verified guarantee.
findings.remediation: Clarify the comment to make the assumption explicit: 'The unconstrained builder seeds a ring, which guarantees connectivity by construction; since BuddyResult carries no connectivity field, we assume this and hardcode connected:true.' Alternatively, reference that this is a documented assumption matching CLAUDE.md.
findings.invariant: The comment must not mislead a maintainer into believing connectivity is measured by the core rather than assumed by the app

findings.theme: Two unrelated constants share the same value, inviting accidental consolidation despite explicit warnings
findings.summary: POLISH_MAX_N and FORCE_TICK_KNEE_N both equal 120 but are unrelated concepts
findings.failure: model.ts line 55 defines POLISH_MAX_N=120 (threshold for auto-disabling polish), and layout.ts line 51 defines FORCE_TICK_KNEE_N=120 (knee for scaling force layout iterations). The comment on line 53-54 explicitly warns 'The value coincides with layout.ts's FORCE_TICK_KNEE_N, an UNRELATED force-tick concept — don't consolidate them.' However, having equal values for unrelated concepts is inherently confusing. A maintainer seeing these equal values might: (1) assume they should stay in sync, (2) try to extract a shared constant, (3) when updating one threshold, accidentally update the other thinking they're related. The equal values contradict the warning not to consolidate.
findings.remediation: Give the constants different values to prevent confusion (even if one is 120 and the other is 119 or 121). The different values themselves would communicate that these are unrelated. Alternatively, add a boundary test that enforces they stay DIFFERENT, not the same.
findings.invariant: When FORCE_TICK_KNEE_N and POLISH_MAX_N are equal, a maintainer is forced to read and trust a comment to know they're unrelated, which is fragile

findings.theme: reopened dialog is not next in tab order from the control that opens it
findings.summary: Reopening the roster-edit dialog via the 'Edit people' button places the dialog's own controls AFTER the entire rest of the running app in Tab order, instead of moving focus into it.
findings.failure: With a graph already on screen (view != null), the JSX in App.tsx renders, in this literal DOM order inside <main>: the {view && (...)} block (stage, #rail with 'Different arrangement'/'Edit people', LayoutToggle, hint, BuddyList — one <button> per roster row — then QualityPanel's Import/Print/Export buttons), and only THEN, as the next sibling, {modalOpen && <RosterModal/>}. Pressing Enter on 'Edit people' sets modalOpen=true but moves DOM focus nowhere (no autoFocus/ref.focus() anywhere in the file — confirmed by grep). Because RosterModal is visually an overlay (#modal { position:absolute; inset:0; z-index:20 } in app.css) but is a LATER DOM sibling, the next Tab press from 'Edit people' does not enter the dialog at all — it advances to LayoutToggle's Ring/Force buttons, then Copy/CSV, then every single buddy-list row button (N of them), then Import/Print/Export, before finally reaching the dialog's textarea. For a 200-person roster that is 200+ Tab presses to reach a dialog that role="dialog" aria-modal="true" claims is already modal-focused. This is the exact 'graph must never be the only interface' contract inverted: the panel path to re-edit the roster is technically reachable but not usably so, and semantically wrong (a screen reader with aria-modal semantics will report content 'inside' a modal that Tab cannot actually reach next).
findings.invariant: When a role="dialog" aria-modal="true" element mounts over existing page content, (a) DOM focus must move to an element inside it, and (b) the set of elements reachable by repeated Tab from that point, before re-entering the dialog, must be empty — no element belonging to the content the dialog overlays may be focusable before the dialog's own first control.
findings.remediation: On RosterModal mount, focus its first field (textarea) with a ref + useEffect, and either render the dialog earlier in DOM order (portal to the top of <main> or document.body) or add a real focus trap so Tab/Shift-Tab cannot leave the dialog while it is open.

findings.theme: focus is not restored when the element that held it unmounts
findings.summary: Closing the roster modal (Generate or Cancel) and the busy overlay (generation finishes or is cancelled) unmount the focused button with no focus restoration, so focus silently reverts to <body>.
findings.failure: handleGenerate/onCancel/applyImported/cancelGeneration (App.tsx lines 60-106) all flip modalOpen or drive bg.status without ever calling .focus() on anything. Trace: user tabs to 'Generate buddy graph' inside RosterModal and presses Enter -> handleGenerate -> setModalOpen(false) -> React unmounts the button that had focus -> the browser resets document.activeElement to <body> (no fallback target exists). The same happens when the busy overlay's 'Cancel' button is pressed (cancelGeneration) or when generation finishes (busy overlay unmounts once bg.status leaves 'running'). A screen-reader user now has to re-discover their place in the page from scratch after every single action that closes an overlay.
findings.invariant: When an element bearing DOM focus is removed from the document by a state transition this app controls, focus must be moved programmatically to a specified, sensible element (e.g. the control that triggered the transition, or the primary heading/landmark of the newly-shown view) — it must never be left to fall back silently to <body>.
findings.remediation: Track the element that had focus before each modal/overlay opens (or just the button that triggered the transition) and call .focus() on a suitable target in the effect/handler that closes it.

findings.theme: an error message renders with no live-region wiring, so it is never announced
findings.summary: A refused roster-file import (bad .txt/.csv drop or 'choose a file' pick) surfaces only as a plain, non-live <div>, unlike the app-level JSON import which is properly announced through the toast's always-mounted role="status" region — so a screen-reader user gets zero spoken feedback that their import failed.
findings.failure:
readFile() (lines 49-56) catches a read failure and calls setFileError(...); it is rendered at line 109 as `{fileError &&
{fileError}
}` with no aria-live, role="alert", or role="status", and it is not associated with the 'choose a file' button via aria-describedby either. Compare with App.tsx's handleImportFile, whose catch calls `flash(...)`, which lands in Notice.tsx's ALREADY-MOUNTED `
` — explicitly designed (per its own comment) so 'a content change in a region it is already watching' is reliably announced. The RosterModal file-read error path was never routed through that same mechanism, so the one error path most likely to be hit early in the exact scenario given ('drop a .txt/.csv file... recover from an error along the way') is invisible to a screen reader: focus stays on the 'choose a file' / drop target, and nothing is spoken.
findings.invariant: Every asynchronous operation whose failure is not announced at the point the user's focus already sits (i.e. the message appears somewhere the user isn't currently reading) must be delivered through a live region (aria-live, role="alert", or an already-mounted role="status" node) so assistive tech announces it without requiring the user to go find it.
findings.remediation: Route RosterModal's fileError (and, for consistency, the file-size/type notes) through the same live-region mechanism the top-level import error uses — e.g. lift it into the shared Notice/toast, or add role="alert" to the `.note.blocking` div.

findings.theme: a control's selected/current state is expressed only visually, not in the accessibility tree
findings.summary: The buddy-list row a keyboard user has selected (which lights up that person's buddies in the graph) is marked only by a CSS class (`.sel`); no `aria-current`/`aria-selected`/`aria-pressed` exposes which row is selected to a screen reader.
findings.failure: `<button key={i} className={"brow" + (selected === i ? " sel" : "")} onClick={() => onSelect(i)}>` (lines 49-53) carries no state attribute at all. Trace the exact 'find one specific person, discover who their buddies are' step: a user tabs through the row buttons and presses Enter on 'Chloe Diaz'. The visual highlight moves; the graph's node/edge classes update (GraphCanvas nodeClass/edgeClass, driven by the same `selected` prop). A screen reader announces only the button's own label text (name + buddies) each time it's focused — never that this particular row IS the current selection versus merely being under the cursor/focus ring. Tabbing away and back gives no way to tell, without vision, which of the N rows is currently selected. This is precisely the class of regression named in this lens's own precedent (a seeded aria-pressed removal passing lint clean) — LayoutToggle.tsx already does this correctly (`aria-pressed={layout === m}` at line 15) but BuddyList's analogous selection state was never given the same treatment.
findings.invariant: For every control whose selected/not-selected visual state differs from its neighbors and drives visible dependent UI elsewhere (here: the graph highlight), the accessible state (aria-current="true" or aria-pressed/aria-selected) must be present and must equal `selected === i` on every render.
findings.remediation: Add `aria-current={selected === i ? "true" : undefined}` (or aria-pressed, matching LayoutToggle's pattern) to the row button in BuddyList.tsx.

findings.theme: a visually-obvious numeric change has no accessible counterpart
findings.summary: The 'Buddies each' stepper's current value is rendered in a plain `<span>` with no aria-live/aria-valuenow, so pressing the +/- buttons produces no spoken confirmation of the new count.
findings.failure: Lines 27-34: two buttons labelled only "fewer buddies"/"more buddies" (aria-label, no reference to the resulting value) flank `{settings.buddies}`, which is plain static content, not a live region and not a role="spinbutton" with aria-valuenow/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax. A screen-reader user pressing '+' repeatedly hears nothing confirming whether the value moved from 4 to 5 or was clamped at BUDDY_MAX (12); they must explicitly navigate to the span to find out.
findings.invariant: Activating a control whose sole effect is to change a displayed numeric value must produce an accessible announcement of the new value (via aria-live on the value node, or role="spinbutton" with aria-valuenow kept in sync with settings.buddies).
findings.remediation: Either wrap the value span in an aria-live="polite" region, or convert the stepper to the native spinbutton pattern with aria-valuenow/min/max mirroring settings.buddies/BUDDY_MIN/BUDDY_MAX.

findings.theme: the settings the app displays and exports are not the settings the graph was actually built with
findings.summary: useBuddyGraph downgrades polish=true to "auto" above POLISH_MAX_N for cost reasons, but `pending.current.settings` was captured BEFORE the downgrade, so viewFromResult stamps the un-downgraded settings onto the GraphView. The Advanced panel then shows Polish "on" for a graph that was never polished, and exportGraph writes `settings.polish: true` into a file whose edges cannot be reproduced from those settings.
findings.failure: Roster of 130 people, Advanced > Polish = on, Generate. Reproduced: the dispatched option is "auto" and the core returns `polished: false`, while `exportGraph(view).settings.polish === true`; feeding those recorded settings back to `buildBuddyGraph(130, 4, {polish: true, seed: 12345})` yields `polished: true` and a DIFFERENT edge list (`JSON.stringify(actual.edges) !== JSON.stringify(claimed.edges)`). The file therefore does not reproduce its own graph. app/test/useBuddyGraph.test.tsx:164 pins only the dispatched request, never the settings recorded on the view, so the suite stays green.
findings.remediation: Compute the effective options once and store THOSE in `pending.current.settings` (e.g. `const effective = { ...settings, polish }` before `pending.current = { names, settings: effective, reroll }`), so the view/export/Advanced panel all describe the graph that was actually built. Ratchet with a test asserting the recorded settings equal the dispatched GenerateRequest.options.
findings.invariant: For every generation, every field of the resulting GraphView.settings equals the corresponding field of the GenerateRequest.options actually posted to the worker (settings.polish === request.options.polish, settings.seed === request.options.seed, settings.minSeparation === request.options.minSeparation, settings.buddies === request.k) — for all n and all settings.

findings.theme: a generation target the core silently demotes is still displayed as if it were applied
findings.summary: `BuddyResult.finalMinSeparation` (the separation the core actually achieved after demotion) is discarded by viewFromResult. The Advanced panel and the exported `settings.minSeparation` keep showing the requested value, so an organizer who sets Min separation = 12 is told 12 was used when the graph was built at 3.
findings.failure: buildBuddyGraph(20, 4, {minSeparation: 12}) returns finalMinSeparation = 3 (also 3 for n=30/k=4, n=12/k=4, n=50/k=6 at the same request). The app displays and exports minSeparation: 12 with no indication it was demoted; nothing in app/test asserts anything about finalMinSeparation.
findings.remediation: Carry `finalMinSeparation` through `viewFromResult` into Metrics (or a `resolvedSettings` field) and surface it wherever minSeparation is displayed — e.g. show the achieved value, or a note when it differs from the request (the parallel of the existing degreeLabel rule: show the produced graph, not the target).
findings.invariant: No generation target rendered as active may differ from the value the core reports it applied: whenever a minSeparation is displayed or exported for a generated GraphView, it equals the BuddyResult.finalMinSeparation of the result that produced that view (or the divergence is explicitly surfaced).

findings.theme: a generation failure that arrives on a channel the hook does not listen to leaves the UI spinning forever
findings.summary: `attach` installs only `worker.onmessage`. There is no `onerror`/`onmessageerror` handler, so a worker that fails to load (wrong Pages `base`, bad MIME, chunk 404) or crashes mid-run never moves the hook out of status "running": the "Generating…" overlay stays up indefinitely, App's whole status==="error" recovery path (toast + reopen modal) never fires, and every subsequent Generate hangs identically with no explanation.
findings.failure: Reproduced with a stub `Worker` whose postMessage never replies: after `generate({n:10,k:4})`, `typeof worker.onerror === "function"` is false, and firing an `error` event on the worker leaves `status === "running"`, `error === null`. Every existing test (appErrorRecovery.test.tsx, useBuddyGraph.test.tsx) mocks `useGenerationWorker` wholesale, so the real hook's failure channels are never exercised — the gap is invisible to the suite.
findings.remediation: In `attach`, also set `worker.onerror` and `worker.onmessageerror` to clear `runningRef` and `setState({status:"error", result:null, error: <message>})`, mirroring the ok:false path. Add a test that dispatches an error event on a stubbed Worker and asserts the hook leaves "running".
findings.invariant: GenState.status never remains "running" after the worker signals failure: for any Worker failure event (`error` or `messageerror`) on the latest run, the hook transitions to status "error" with a non-empty error string.

findings.theme: a connectivity fact the quality score depends on is assumed rather than measured on the generation path
findings.summary: `viewFromResult` hardcodes `connected: true` and `largestComponentFraction: 1` for every generated graph, while `assembleMetrics` gates aspl/diameter/quality on exactly that flag. The import path measures both with the core's own functions; the generation path does not. If a generated graph is ever disconnected, ASPL is a reachable-pairs mean that beats the whole-n Moore bound, so the gauge can read up to 100% and the caption "everyone's well-linked" for a roster split in two — the precise failure the import path was hardened against.
findings.failure: Not reproducible today: a scan of n=3..40, k=2..10 with minSeparation in {2,3,5,12} found no disconnected buildBuddyGraph output (the ring seed guarantees it by construction, and polish penalizes disconnection). The defect is that nothing in the app or its suite would detect a regression — the false 100%/"well-linked" display would appear with no test failing, because the connectivity input is a literal rather than a measurement.
findings.remediation: Lib-first, as app/CLAUDE.md already notes: add `connected` and `largestComponentFraction` to `BuddyResult` (the core already computes `allPairsSummary`, whose Summary carries `connected`) and pass them through `viewFromResult`, so both GraphView producers measure rather than assert. Until then, a test that rebuilds a Graph from `r.edges` and asserts the view's connectivity fields match `allPairsSummary`/`largestComponentFraction` closes the detection gap.
findings.invariant: For every GraphView v produced by either producer, v.metrics.connected === allPairsSummary(Graph built from v.edges over v.names.length).connected and v.metrics.largestComponentFraction === largestComponentFraction(that graph) — and consequently v.metrics.quality === 0 whenever the graph is disconnected.

findings.theme: a single selected/hovered slot currently encodes exactly one interaction concept (whose neighbors to glow / which row to emphasize), and F10's two-endpoint interaction cannot be added by widening that slot without every existing consumer becoming mode-aware
findings.summary: `selected`/`onSelect` is threaded unconditionally from App.tsx to both GraphCanvas.tsx (line 140-144, drives the single-node neighbor-glow `focus` at GraphCanvas.tsx:177) and BuddyList.tsx (line 160, drives per-row `sel` styling and its own click-to-select at BuddyList.tsx:51-52). F10 (path finder) needs a second, independent selection concept — two path endpoints, picked either on the canvas or (per the stated 'graph is a view, never the only interface' principle) from the keyboard-navigable BuddyList table. Implementing that by reusing the existing `selected`/`onSelect` prop would overload one click handler with two live meanings (navigate-to-person vs. pick-path-endpoint) in both consumers simultaneously; the honest fix is a distinct picking-mode state (e.g. `pathPick: {a, b} | null`) threaded to both GraphCanvas and BuddyList, each gaining a mode branch in their click handlers, not a reuse of `selected`. This is expected fan-out for a real two-endpoint feature (not a hidden coupling violation — both components legitimately need to reflect app-wide interaction state per the app's own 'graph is a view, never the only interface' rule), but it is real, touches both view components plus App.tsx, and is easy to miss if `selected` is naively repurposed.
findings.failure: If path-endpoint picking is wired through the existing `onSelect`/`selected` prop instead of a new mode-aware state, clicking a node while picking path endpoint #2 will also silently reassign BuddyList's row highlight and GraphCanvas's neighbor-glow focus to that node, producing a UI where the 'selected person' context (used elsewhere for buddy-list emphasis) flips mid-pick with no way to distinguish it from a normal navigation click.
findings.remediation: Add a dedicated path-endpoint state (own hook, e.g. `usePathFinder`, following the existing useBuddyGraph/useGenerationWorker/useNotice extraction pattern) and a `pickMode`/`path` prop pair to both GraphCanvas and BuddyList, so endpoint-picking clicks are structurally distinct from the existing single-select click path rather than overloading it.
findings.invariant: For every value the selected/hovered slot can encode, each of its consumers (grep `selected|onSelect|hovered|onHover` in app/src) interprets a click the same way regardless of any picking mode; adding a second concurrent interaction concept (path endpoints) without a mode discriminant breaks this for at least one consumer.

findings.theme: F10's explicit acceptance criterion (ESC clears) has no existing analog anywhere in the codebase to extend from
findings.summary: PROJECT_PLAN.md F10 (line 121) requires 'ESC clears'. Grepping app/src for `Escape|onKeyDown|keydown` returns zero matches — there is no global key-listener pattern anywhere in the app to hang this off of (RosterModal, GraphCanvas, and every panel are pointer/click driven only). Implementing F10 means introducing the app's first global keyboard-escape handling from scratch in the composition root, deciding what it clears when multiple things could be open (modal vs. path-pick vs. selection) — a genuinely new piece of app infrastructure, not a one-line addition to an existing seam.
findings.failure: Absent this, an engineer implementing F10 has no existing pattern to follow or extend and may bind ESC narrowly (e.g. only inside GraphCanvas's SVG, which per its own comment at GraphCanvas.tsx:208-214 is deliberately NOT a keyboard focus stop), so a keyboard user tabbed into BuddyList picking path endpoints could not clear the pick via ESC at all.
findings.remediation: Add one document-level keydown listener in App.tsx (or a small `useEscape` hook) that clears whichever transient UI state (modal, path pick, selection) is currently front-most, established as the one place ESC semantics live before F10, F7, or F8's own modal/panel needs multiply it.
findings.invariant: For every dismissible transient UI state the app introduces (modal open, path-pick in progress, future constraint-row editing), pressing ESC while it is active clears it — grep-checkable today by the absence of any Escape handling at all.

findings.theme: the ego/focus-layout extension seam in GraphCanvas has no live caller and any further hardening of it for F10 or F8 would repeat the documented anti-pattern
findings.summary: `LAYOUT_MODES`/`FIT_MODES`/`positionsFor` (GraphCanvas.tsx:6-42) is pre-hardened for a future selection-keyed layout mode ('F8 focus') that is not in F8's actual acceptance criteria and has no caller anywhere in app/src (grep for a third LayoutMode confirms only "ring"/"force" exist). F10 (path finder) does not need a new layout mode at all — it only needs to highlight a subset of existing positions/edges, which `positionsFor` has no bearing on. Filed as deferral per the review's own hard rule; not gating, and specifically not re-litigating the already-converged 6-round/8-finding record in app/CLAUDE.md's Known follow-ons.
findings.failure: N/A — no caller exists; this is a recorded non-finding, not a reproduced defect.
findings.remediation: None needed now. If a selection-dependent layout is ever actually built, resolve it against the four concrete unresolved items app/CLAUDE.md already lists (focus-on-hover re-layout snapping, radius clipping past FIT_MODES' frame, undefined empty-selection focus, and positionsFor's new parameter touching graphCanvasFit.test.ts) rather than re-deriving them.
findings.invariant: grep -n '"ring" \| "force"' app/src/graph/GraphCanvas.tsx shows LayoutMode has exactly two live variants; no third variant is referenced anywhere in app/src.

findings.theme: Garbled prose in a docstring misleads reader about the invariant being enforced
findings.summary: The phrase 'finite reachable-pairs mean' is incomplete and grammatically broken, leaving the documented invariant unintelligible to a future contributor
findings.failure: Line 98-100 reads: 'This alone does not catch a disconnected-but-edged graph (finite reachable-pairs mean); `assembleMetrics` gates that on `connected`.' The phrase 'finite reachable-pairs mean' is a sentence fragment and does not complete a grammatically coherent thought.
findings.remediation: Replace the garbled phrase with something like: 'This alone does not catch a disconnected-but-edged graph (ASPL over reachable pairs within a component is finite); `assembleMetrics` gates that on `connected`.' The intent is to explain that a finite ASPL alone cannot prove connectivity—a disconnected graph with edges has finite ASPL over reachable pairs within each component—so we also check the `connected` flag.
findings.invariant: Every prose comment describing code behavior must be grammatically complete and parse unambiguously to a reader who does not already understand the code

findings.theme: the setup dialog claims modal semantics (role=dialog aria-modal=true) but nothing in the tree actually manages focus for it — no trap, no initial focus, no restore on close — so a keyboard user can tab straight through it into covered background controls, or lose their place entirely when it opens/closes
findings.summary: RosterModal is rendered as a plain sibling AFTER the live-graph fragment in App.tsx's `<main>` (view fragment first at line 132, `{modalOpen && <RosterModal .../>}` at line 165). When the modal is opened over an existing graph (click 'Edit people', App.tsx:153), the modal's own controls (textarea, file buttons, settings, Cancel/Generate) sit LAST in DOM/tab order — AFTER the rail buttons, the ring/force toggle, every buddy-list row (up to MAX_ROSTER_N=1000), and the quality-panel buttons, all of which remain fully rendered and focusable underneath the opaque overlay (app.css:140 `#modal{position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:20;background:rgba(...,0.72)}` sits above `#rail`/`#toggle`/`#buddies`/`#metrics` at z-index 4). RosterModal.tsx has no autoFocus, no Escape handler, and no Tab/Shift+Tab containment (grepped the whole app/src tree for Escape/autoFocus/inert/focus()/tabIndex/trapFocus/<dialog>: zero hits; package.json has no focus-trap dependency). App.tsx also never restores focus to the trigger (`Edit people`/`Import`) or moves it into the dialog when it opens/closes, so a screen-reader-and-mouseless user pressing Tab after opening 'Edit people' walks through the entire covered background UI before ever reaching the dialog they just opened, and after Generate/Cancel closes it, focus is silently dropped to <body> with no cue where it went.
findings.failure: Press the 'Edit people' button (keyboard, Enter). The dialog visually covers the screen. Press Tab: focus moves to the ring/force layout toggle and buddy-list rows underneath the overlay, NOT into the dialog's textarea — the dialog's own first control isn't reached until every background control has been tabbed through. On Cancel/Generate, focus lands on <body> with no re-announcement of what's now on screen.
findings.remediation: Give RosterModal an initial-focus effect (focus the textarea or first control on mount), implement a real Tab/Shift+Tab focus trap scoped to the dialog subtree (or use `inert`/`aria-hidden` + `tabIndex=-1` sweep on the background while open), add an Escape handler that calls onCancel when canCancel, and restore focus to the element that opened the dialog (Edit people / Import) when it closes.
findings.invariant: While an element with role=dialog and aria-modal=true is open, every element outside its subtree must be excluded from the Tab sequence (unfocusable), and on open/close focus must be inside the dialog / restored to a well-defined element — never left on a background element or dropped to <body>.

findings.theme: the only signal that generation started, is running, or finished is visual text with no live region and no focus movement, so the core 'generate a graph' step is silent for a screen-reader user
findings.summary:
`handleGenerate` (App.tsx:60-66) closes the modal (`setModalOpen(false)`) the instant `bg.generate()` is called — before the async worker result arrives — so the element that had focus (the 'Generate buddy graph' button) is unmounted immediately and focus drops to (see prior finding). The busy overlay that appears in its place (`
…Generating…
`, App.tsx:176-181) has no `role="status"`/`aria-live` and is a fresh DOM node (not a persistently-mounted region, unlike Notice.tsx, whose own comment explicitly documents why that distinction matters: 'Unmounting the region and remounting it with text is announced far less reliably'). When generation finishes, the busy overlay is replaced by the full view (stage/rail/toggle/buddylist/qualitypanel) with no live region announcing completion and no focus movement into the new content either.
findings.failure: Screen-reader user fills the roster, presses Enter/clicks Generate. Focus is dropped to <body>. Nothing is announced: not 'Generating…', not a failure, not success. The only way to learn anything happened is to start tabbing from the top of the page again and discover either the graph UI or a reopened modal by trial.
findings.remediation: Wrap the busy state's status text in a persistently-mounted `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"` region (mounted before text changes, same pattern already used in Notice.tsx), and move focus to a sensible landmark (e.g. the rail's person-count, or the Cancel button) when the busy overlay mounts, and to the graph rail / re-opened modal when the transition resolves.
findings.invariant: Every transition between {modal open, busy/running, view rendered, error} that is communicated to sighted users only via mounted/unmounted text must also be announced via a live region that exists in the DOM before its text changes, independent of where focus happens to be.

findings.theme: a visually-obvious state change (which buddy-list row is selected/highlighted) has no accessible counterpart, even though the app's own design says the graph is only a view and the buddy list is the authoritative keyboard interface for it
findings.summary: Each buddy-list row is `<button className={"brow" + (selected === i ? " sel" : "")} onClick={() => onSelect(i)}>`. Selecting a row only changes a CSS class; there is no `aria-current`, `aria-pressed`, or `aria-selected` reflecting `selected === i`. GraphCanvas.tsx:220 explicitly documents the graph as `role="img"` whose label tells assistive tech to 'Use the buddy list for a keyboard-navigable view' — i.e. the buddy list is declared the canonical accessible surface for selection. But unlike LayoutToggle.tsx (line 15, `aria-pressed={layout === m}` — correctly done, in the same codebase), BuddyList never exposes which row is selected. A screen-reader user who activates a row to 'find one specific person' and highlight their buddies in the graph gets no confirmation of which name is now selected; re-visiting the list later gives no way to determine the current selection at all via the accessibility tree.
findings.failure: Tab to a buddy-list row, press Enter to select a person (e.g. row 5). The graph nodes visually re-highlight. A screen-reader user gets a normal 'button' press announcement but nothing telling them selection succeeded or which row is now current; navigating away and back to the list, no attribute on any row indicates row 5 is selected.
findings.remediation: Add `aria-current={selected === i}` (or `aria-pressed`) to each buddy row, mirroring the pattern already used correctly in LayoutToggle.tsx.
findings.invariant: For every row i in the buddy list, the DOM exposes selected===i via an ARIA state attribute (aria-current/aria-pressed/aria-selected) on that row's element — never via CSS class alone.

findings.theme: a control's tab-order position doesn't match its fixed on-screen position, so a keyboard-only user following visual order can't reach it without traversing everything else first
findings.summary: `<Notice message={notice} onDismiss={clear} />` is the very last element rendered in App.tsx (after the hidden file `<input>`, itself after `<Slips>`), but the toast is styled `position: fixed; top: 14px; left: 50%` (app.css:166) — visually pinned above every other control on the page. Every flash/error toast (import failure, reroll-gate refusal, 'already optimal' notice, worker error when a view exists) therefore places its dismiss button dead last in the Tab sequence: after the rail buttons, the layout toggle, every buddy-list row (up to 1000 for a full roster), and the quality-panel buttons. A sighted keyboard-only user (motor-impaired, not using a screen reader) sees the toast appear at the top of the screen but must Tab through the entire rest of the UI to reach and dismiss it by keyboard; on a large roster the toast will very likely have already auto-cleared (`AUTO_CLEAR_MS`=4000 in useNotice.ts) before they can Tab that far.
findings.failure: With a 200-person roster loaded, trigger a reroll-gate refusal (e.g. via a settings combination `rerollBlockReason` refuses). The toast appears fixed at the top of the screen. Pressing Tab from the rail's 'Different arrangement' button does not reach the toast's dismiss button until ~200+ Tab presses later (after every buddy row and the quality-panel buttons), by which point the 4-second auto-clear has almost certainly already removed it.
findings.remediation: Render Notice earlier in the DOM (e.g. immediately inside #app, before #stage/#rail) so its position in the Tab sequence matches its fixed visual position, independent of roster size.
findings.invariant: For any element with a fixed/sticky visual position, its position in DOM/Tab order should not require traversing a roster-size-dependent (unbounded) number of other focusable elements to reach it.

findings.theme: a status change communicated only by mutating the accessible name of the currently-focused control, with no live region, is not reliably announced by assistive tech
findings.summary: `<button className="chipbtn" onClick={copyAll}>{copied ? "Copied" : "Copy"}</button>` changes its own accessible name from 'Copy' to 'Copied' for 1100ms (`setTimeout(() => setCopied(false), 1100)`) with no `aria-live`/`role=status` anywhere in the vicinity and no focus movement. This is the same class of unreliability Notice.tsx's own comment calls out for a different case ('Unmounting the region and remounting it with text is announced far less reliably') — here it's not even a live region at all, just an unannounced label mutation on the focused element, so most screen readers give no confirmation the copy succeeded.
findings.failure: Tab to the 'Copy' button in the buddy panel, press Enter. Visually the label flips to 'Copied' for 1.1s. A screen-reader user commonly hears nothing confirming success (behavior varies by AT/browser, hence PLAUSIBLE not CONFIRMED — I did not have a real AT to verify announcement, only that no live-region/focus-management primitive exists to make it reliable).
findings.remediation: Wrap the copy confirmation in a `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"` region (reusing the Notice pattern) rather than relying solely on the focused button's label text changing.
findings.invariant: caseOnly — announcement reliability of a focused-element label mutation is AT/browser-dependent behavior, not something this codebase can assert a hard pass/fail on without a real AT harness; filed for awareness, does not gate.

findings.theme: a dropped file is accepted as roster text whatever it actually is, so the app's own export file silently becomes a roster of fake people
findings.summary: The roster drop handler performs no file-type check, while the file picker beside it declares accept=".txt,.csv,text/plain,text/csv". `accept` does not apply to drops, so the drop path admits a strictly larger file set than the picker — including the app's own exported buddygraph.json, whose raw text parseRoster happily shreds into "names". There is no drag-and-drop import path for a graph file, so the natural gesture ("reload the graph I exported") lands here and is misinterpreted rather than refused or routed to importGraph.
findings.failure: Reproduced with @testing-library/react against the real RosterModal: exportGraphJson of a 6-person graph (viewFromResult(['Alice','Bob','Cara','Dan','Eve','Fay'], DEFAULT_SETTINGS, buildBuddyGraph(6,2,{seed:1,polish:false}))) written to a File('buddygraph.json', type 'application/json') and dispatched via fireEvent.drop on `.sheet`. Result: the counter renders "44 people", the Generate button is enabled (disabled === false), and clicking it calls onGenerate with names = ["{", "\"version\": 1", "\"people\": [", "\"id\": 0", "\"name\": \"Alice\"", "}", "\"id\": 1", ...] — 44 entries — alongside the warning `Removed 34 duplicate entries ({, }, ], [, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5). Each person appears once.` The organizer can then print buddy slips for a person named `"version": 1`. The same hole admits a binary file under the 8 MB gate (readAsText mojibake). No existing test dispatches a drop event on RosterModal, so the whole path is uncovered.
findings.remediation: Gate `readFile` in RosterModal on the same set the picker declares — accept only text/plain, text/csv, or a .txt/.csv extension — and surface the existing `fileError` note for anything else, so the drop path and the picker path admit exactly one file set. Better still, detect a parsed `{version: 1, people: [...]}` object and route it to `importGraph` (App.applyImported) instead, which turns the most likely mistake into the action the user meant.
findings.invariant: For every File f, the roster drop handler replaces the roster text iff f is in the accepted-roster-type set declared by the picker's `accept` attribute (text/plain | text/csv | .txt | .csv); for every f outside that set the roster text is unchanged and a notice is raised. In particular, no file whose text JSON.parses to an object with version === 1 and an array `people` may ever reach parseRoster.

findings.theme: a file dropped outside the roster sheet triggers browser default navigation and discards the unsaved graph
findings.summary: `onDragOver`/`onDrop` with preventDefault exist only on `.sheet`. Nothing guards the `#modal` backdrop, `#stage`, the rail, or the document, and when no modal is open there is no drop handler anywhere. A dropped file therefore reaches the browser default action, which navigates the tab to the file — destroying the in-memory roster, graph, and settings, none of which are persisted.
findings.failure: Traced by grep: the only dragover/drop handlers in app/src are RosterModal.tsx:70 on `.sheet`. With a graph on screen and the modal closed, dropping buddygraph.json anywhere in the viewport hits the UA default (navigate to the dropped file) rather than any app handler; the App holds `view`, `names`, `settings`, `layout` only in React state, so the whole session is lost with no confirmation. Marked PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED because jsdom does not implement the navigation default, so the consequence is derived from the HTML drag-and-drop spec rather than observed here.
findings.remediation: Add a document-level (or #app-level) dragover/drop listener that preventDefaults unconditionally, and route a dropped file to the appropriate importer by kind — roster text to setRoster, a version-1 BuddyGraph JSON to applyImported — so no drop can reach the UA default.
findings.invariant: Any `drop` event carrying `dataTransfer.files`, dispatched on any node in the document, ends with `event.defaultPrevented === true`.

findings.theme: a worker failure that is not a thrown exception inside onmessage leaves the UI permanently in the running state with no error surfaced
findings.summary: `attach` wires only `worker.onmessage`. The Worker's own `error` and `messageerror` channels are unhandled, so a failure that prevents the worker script from ever posting a message (module-load failure on a stale deploy where the hashed worker chunk 404s, a CSP worker-src refusal, an OOM during instantiation) never transitions state. `status` stays "running" indefinitely, App renders the `Generating…` overlay forever, and the App error effect — which keys entirely off `bg.status === "error"` — never fires, so no toast appears and the documented recovery path (reopen the setup modal on a first-generation failure) never runs.
findings.failure: Traced: the only `onerror` in app/src is FileReader's in readFileText.ts:19; there is no `worker.onerror` or `worker.onmessageerror` anywhere. The try/catch in generate.worker.ts only covers exceptions thrown *inside* a delivered onmessage, i.e. exactly the failures that already have a response path. For a worker that never runs its module, `runningRef.current` stays true, `setState({status:'running'})` is never superseded, and the App effect's `if (bg.status === "error")` branch is dead. The user's only escape is the Cancel button (bg.cancel → reset), and on a first generation the modal reopens only because cancelGeneration checks `!view` — the error itself is never reported. appErrorRecovery.test.tsx exercises the error branch only by mocking useGenerationWorker's state directly, so it cannot catch the missing transition.
findings.remediation: In `attach`, also set `worker.onerror` and `worker.onmessageerror` to clear runningRef and setState({status:'error', result:null, error: <message>}) — mirroring the ok:false branch — so every way a worker can fail converges on the one state the App already knows how to recover from.
findings.invariant: After any error event on the generation Worker (an ok:false response, an `error` event, or a `messageerror` event) GenState.status === 'error' and GenState.error is a non-empty string; GenState.status === 'running' is reachable only while a computation can still deliver a result.

findings.theme: first/second-degree neighbor computation is embedded privately in the view component instead of a shared pure function
findings.summary: GraphCanvas.tsx:178-188 computes the 1st-order (`first`) and 2nd-order (`second`) buddy Sets from `adjacency` inline inside the component, memoized on `focus` (hover/select) — it's the only implementation of this traversal anywhere in app/src (grepped; no shared helper exists). F8's node-explorer panel (PROJECT_PLAN.md:106, 'buddies (1st), reachable-in-2 (2nd)') needs the identical computation but driven by an explicitly-opened/searched node, independent of GraphCanvas's hover state and rendering lifecycle — it cannot call into GraphCanvas's private `useMemo`. Implementing F8 as specified either duplicates this BFS-adjacency-walk logic in the new explorer component (violating the project's own DRY/'one view model' principle and the 'UI never reimplements [graph] math... add it to the core' framing is moot here since this part is legitimately app-side, but duplicating it in two places is still a real seam gap) or forces a refactor of GraphCanvas to extract and export it — neither is free, and neither was anticipated by any comment in the file (unlike the FIT_MODES/positionsFor seam, which explicitly anticipates F8's *layout* needs but says nothing about this *panel-data* need).
findings.failure: Building NodeExplorer against the current code means either copy-pasting the Set-building loop from GraphCanvas.tsx:180-186 into a new panel file (two divergeable copies of 'first/second-order neighbors of vertex i'), or reaching into GraphCanvas internals that aren't exported.
findings.invariant: For any UI consumer that needs the first/second-degree buddy sets of a vertex from `adjacency`, there is exactly one implementation all such consumers call — not one instance embedded per component.
findings.remediation: Extract the first/second-degree computation (GraphCanvas.tsx:178-188) into a pure, exported function (e.g. `graph/neighbors.ts` or alongside `model.ts`) taking `(adjacency, focus)` and returning `{first, second}`; have both GraphCanvas and the new NodeExplorer call it, before either duplicates the logic.

findings.theme: the highlight-class functions assume exactly one active highlight concern and have no seam for a second, simultaneous one
findings.summary: `nodeClass`/`edgeClass` (GraphCanvas.tsx:192-205) compute ONE mutually-exclusive className per node/edge from a single `focus` value (hover-or-select) via an if/else chain (sel/hi/hi2/faded and edge/lit/lit2/dim). F10 (path finder) needs to render an independent highlight — the shortest-chain edges/nodes between two selected people — that can be active at the same time as (or instead of) the existing hover-glow.
