There is no isolated extension point: adding path-highlighting means editing the branches of both functions to reconcile two simultaneous, potentially-conflicting highlight sources (e.g., is a node on the path AND second-degree-from-hover rendered as 'hi2' or as 'on-path'? which wins?), not adding an orthogonal case the way FIT_MODES/positionsFor's `assertNever` pattern allows for layout modes.
findings.failure: Attempting to add a `path: Set<number>` / `pathEdges: Set<string>` prop and folding it into `nodeClass`/`edgeClass` as written requires new precedence logic inside the existing conditional chain, not a clean additive branch — the functions have to be restructured (e.g., into a composable class-builder) rather than extended.
findings.invariant: Adding a second, independent highlight concern does not require editing the existing branches of nodeClass/edgeClass for the first concern.
findings.remediation: Before building F10's rendering, refactor nodeClass/edgeClass from a single-focus if/else into a small composable model (e.g., accumulate applicable class tokens per concern — hover-adjacency, path-membership, selection — and join them) so path-highlighting is an additive concern, not a rewrite of the hover logic.

findings.theme: F10 needs an actual shortest path (vertex sequence), but the core only exposes distances, so a naive app-side implementation would violate the project's own 'no BFS in app/' rule
findings.summary: `bfsDistances` (lib/src/core/metrics.ts:10, re-exported via lib/src/core/index.ts:16) returns only a distance vector, with no predecessor tracking — there is no core function that reconstructs an actual shortest path (an ordered vertex list) between two nodes, and none is exported. F10's acceptance criterion is explicit: 'path matches BFS; ties broken deterministically.' Building this against `view.buddies` (adjacency) in app/src without a core addition means writing BFS-with-predecessor-tracking (real graph-search algorithm code, including the tie-break rule) inside app/, directly violating app/CLAUDE.md's 'The UI never reimplements math... No BFS/ASPL/Moore code in app/. If a number is missing, add it to the core (lib-first), not here.' The correct path is real fan-out into lib/ (new function + export + property/oracle-parity tests per lib/CLAUDE.md's 'change the Python first' rule) that must land, build, and be published to lib/dist before app/ can consume it — a two-package sequencing cost, not a same-repo one-file change.
findings.failure: A developer under time pressure reconstructing the path locally in app/src via `adjacency` (e.g. a home-grown BFS+predecessor walk in a new `panels/PathFinder.tsx`) would satisfy F10's acceptance test today but plant graph-search logic in the UI layer that the project's own architecture doc forbids, and whose tie-break rule could silently diverge from the core's determinism contract.
findings.invariant: No file under app/src performs a graph traversal (BFS/DFS/shortest-path) over `adjacency`/`edges` from scratch; every such traversal result is obtained by calling a `ringweave` core export.
findings.remediation: Add a `shortestPath(g, source, target): number[] | null` (or `bfsPredecessors`) function to lib/src/core/metrics.ts with a documented, deterministic tie-break (matching the reference Python), export it from lib/src/core/index.ts, add property/oracle-parity tests, rebuild lib/dist, then have F10's UI call it — before the app-only shortcut gets written.

findings.theme: the composition root inlines cross-cutting UI state instead of following its own established hook-extraction convention
findings.summary: App.tsx already extracts cohesive state into hooks for notice (`useNotice`) and generation (`useBuddyGraph`/`useGenerationWorker`), but selection state (`selected`, `hovered`, and the paired `resetSelection` reset-on-every-graph-replacing-action logic at App.tsx:36-58) is inlined directly in the component with no equivalent hook. F8 adds search-query state, an explorer open/closed flag, and a back-stack of visited nodes; F10 adds a path-finder mode with two selected endpoints and an ESC-clears listener. All of that is selection-adjacent and, on the current trajectory, would land as more inline `useState`s in App.tsx rather than following the hook-extraction pattern the file already models elsewhere — growing the composition root inconsistently with its own convention rather than by it.
findings.failure: No concrete failure yet (F8/F10 don't exist) — this is a structural risk observed by tracing where the next two committed features' state would naturally land given the current file's shape, not a present defect.
findings.invariant: Every piece of cross-cutting UI state in App.tsx with its own reset/clear semantics (notice, generation, and — by the same logic — selection) is owned by a dedicated hook, consistent with the pattern the file already uses for notice and generation.
findings.remediation: Extract `selected`/`hovered`/`resetSelection` into a `useSelection` hook now (small, low-risk, matches existing convention), so F8's explorer/back-stack and F10's path-mode state have an established place to compose into rather than accreting as ad hoc useStates in App.tsx.

findings.theme: role=dialog aria-modal=true is asserted in markup but never enforced in behavior: focus is never moved into the dialog on open, never restored on close, and the background is never made inert
findings.summary: RosterModal renders `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` but no effect ever calls .focus() on any element inside it, and App.tsx never restores focus to the triggering control when the dialog closes. Worse, when the dialog is reopened via the 'Edit people' button (App.tsx:153) while a graph already exists, RosterModal is inserted into the DOM AFTER the live graph UI (App.tsx:132-173: `{view && (...)}` block precedes `{modalOpen && <RosterModal/>}`), and nothing marks that live UI inert or removes it from the tab sequence.
findings.failure: From a cold load: click 'Generate buddy graph' -> focus was on that button, which unmounts -> the browser drops focus to <body>, and nothing announces or moves focus to the newly-visible graph/rail/quality panel; a screen-reader user hears nothing and must re-navigate from the top of the page. Reproduce the worse case: with a graph already generated, press Tab from the 'Edit people' button. Because RosterModal is the LAST element under <main> in DOM order, Tab walks through LayoutToggle's Ring/Force buttons, every BuddyList row, and QualityPanel's Import/Print/Export buttons -- all of which are still live and mutate app state -- before ever reaching the reopened dialog's textarea. A keyboard user can also Tab out of the 'modal' entirely (no trap) into the live graph controls while it is nominally open, and can dismiss the underlying Notice toast or trigger CSV export while the setup sheet sits open on top.
findings.remediation: On RosterModal mount, move focus to the first focusable element (e.g. the textarea) and, on unmount, restore focus to the element that opened it (store the triggering element in a ref before setModalOpen(true)). Move RosterModal earlier in the DOM (or use a portal) so it's the first thing after the header, and mark the rest of <main> inert (or aria-hidden + tabindex=-1 on its interactive descendants) while the dialog is open.

findings.theme: a control's visually-obvious selected state has no accessible-tree counterpart
findings.summary: Each row in the buddy list is a `<button className={"brow" + (selected === i ? " sel" : "")}>` — selection is communicated purely through a CSS class. No `aria-current`, `aria-pressed`, or `aria-selected` is set, so a screen-reader user who activates a row (to 'find one specific person' and see it highlighted in the graph, per GraphCanvas's own `nodeClass`/`edgeClass` glow) gets no auditory confirmation of which person is currently selected, nor any way to query it later without re-activating every row.
findings.failure: Tab to a BuddyList row, press Enter to select a person (App.tsx setSelected -> GraphCanvas highlights them and their buddies). NVDA/VoiceOver announces only the button's name and buddy text — never 'selected'/'current'. Tabbing to a different, unselected row announces exactly the same way, so the two states are indistinguishable by ear.
findings.remediation: Add `aria-current={selected === i ? "true" : undefined}` (or `aria-selected` if the list is given `role="listbox"`/`role="list"` with `role="option"` rows) to each `.brow` button so the accessibility tree tracks the same state the `sel` class already tracks.
findings.invariant: for every BuddyList row button i, the presence of aria-current="true" (or aria-selected="true") on that button is exactly (selected === i) — i.e. the accessible selected-state flag and the `sel` CSS class are computed from, and therefore always agree with, the same predicate.

findings.theme: inline error/refusal text is rendered into ordinary DOM with no live region, so it is invisible to a screen reader unless the user happens to tab or re-read to it
findings.summary: `fileError`, `inputCapped`, `parsed.warnings`, and `feas.messages` (the exact set of error/empty/infeasible-settings paths the scenario calls out: a refused import, an infeasible buddies/roster-size combination) are rendered as plain `<div className="note">` / `<div className="note blocking">` elements with no `role="alert"`, `role="status"`, or `aria-live` anywhere, and the disabled 'Generate buddy graph' button (line 104) has no `aria-describedby` pointing at them. Contrast with Notice.tsx, which the codebase's own comments show was deliberately built as a persistently-mounted `role="status"` region for exactly this reason — that treatment was never extended to RosterModal's own notices.
findings.failure: Drop a corrupt file onto the roster textarea, or set 'Buddies each' above what the roster size supports via the stepper. `fileError`/`feas.messages` appear in the DOM and the Generate button becomes `disabled`, but nothing is announced. A screen-reader user who isn't currently reading that part of the sheet has no way to learn the generate action is blocked, or why, without manually re-exploring the dialog after each edit.
findings.remediation: Wrap the notices region in a persistently-mounted `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"` container (mirroring Notice.tsx's own established pattern), or at minimum add `aria-describedby` from the Generate button to the blocking message ids so a screen-reader user hears the reason when they reach the disabled button.
findings.invariant: whenever fileError, inputCapped, or a feas.canGenerate===false message is non-empty, the DOM element rendering it is inside a container that already existed with role=status/alert or aria-live before the text changed (never a freshly-mounted node), so its appearance is reliably announced.

findings.theme: a state transition with clear visual feedback (the busy overlay) has no accessible-tree announcement
findings.summary:
The generating overlay (`{bg.status === "running" &&
...Generating…...`) has no `role="status"`/`aria-live` and focus is never moved to its Cancel button. Unlike Notice.tsx (a persistently-mounted live region built specifically so state changes are announced), this overlay is a plain conditionally-mounted div, so its appearance is not guaranteed to be announced, and a screen-reader user who wants to cancel a slow generation has no way to discover the Cancel button exists without already knowing to tab to it.
findings.failure: Click 'Generate buddy graph' on a large roster with polish on (a genuinely slow path per lib docs). The overlay mounts with 'Generating…' and a Cancel button, but a screen-reader user gets no announcement that generation started or that a Cancel control now exists; they'd only find it by blindly tabbing forward from wherever focus ended up (which, per the dialog-focus finding above, is <body>).
findings.remediation: Give the busy overlay `role="status" aria-live="polite"` (or reuse the Notice pattern) and consider moving focus to its Cancel button when it mounts.
findings.invariant: whenever bg.status transitions to "running", an assistive-technology-visible announcement of that transition occurs without requiring the user to move focus first.

findings.theme: a documented capability (import a previously exported graph) has no control reachable from the state the scenario starts in
findings.summary: The only control that opens the JSON-import file picker is `QualityPanel`'s 'Import ↑' button (`onImport={() => importRef.current?.click()}`), and `QualityPanel` is only rendered inside `{view && (...)}` (App.tsx:132-163). On a cold load, `view` is `null` and `modalOpen` is `true` showing only `RosterModal`, which offers no JSON-import affordance (its own file control at RosterModal.tsx:85-97 is scoped to `.txt/.csv` roster text, not `GraphView` JSON — verified via its `accept=".txt,.csv,text/plain,text/csv"` and `readFile`/`parseRoster` call path, distinct from App.tsx's `importGraph`/`JSON.parse` path). There is no keyboard (or mouse) path from a cold load straight to loading an exported `.json` graph; the user is forced to type/paste some roster and successfully generate first.
findings.failure: Fresh page load (no roster yet). A user who has a previously exported buddygraph.json and wants to reload it has no reachable control to do so — 'Import ↑' does not exist anywhere in the DOM until after a first successful generation, at which point importing simply replaces that throwaway graph.
findings.remediation: Add a JSON-import entry point to RosterModal itself (e.g. a 'Load exported graph' button alongside 'choose a file'/'try example names') so the capability is reachable before any roster has been generated, matching the CLAUDE.md invariant that 'everything ... works from the panels' regardless of starting state.
findings.invariant: the control that triggers loading a previously exported GraphView JSON is present in the DOM (and thus reachable by Tab) at every point in the app's lifecycle, including immediately after a cold load with view === null.
